translations.literal: Biographies 2, Empresses and Consorts (Part 2): ○ Empress Qinci of Emperor Ruizong, Empress Zhenyi of Emperor Ruizong, Empress Zhaode of Emperor Shizong, First Consort Zhang of Emperor Shizong, First Consort Li of Emperor Shizong, Empress Xiaoyi of Emperor Xianzong, Empress Zhaosheng of Emperor Xianzong, Empress Qinhuai of Emperor Zhangzong, First Consort Li of Emperor Zhangzong, Queen Tudan of Emperor Weishao, Empress Wang of Emperor Xuanzong, Empress Minghui of Emperor Xuanzong, Empress Tudan of Emperor Aizong

sentences.zh: 睿宗欽慈皇后，蒲察氏。

translations.literal: Empress Qinci of Emperor Ruizong, of the Pucha clan.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Qinci of Emperor Ruizong was of the Pucha clan.

sentences.zh: 睿宗元配。

translations.literal: She was Emperor Ruizong's primary consort.
translations.idiomatic: She was Emperor Ruizong's primary consort.

sentences.zh: 后之母，太祖之妹也。

translations.literal: The empress's mother was a younger sister of Emperor Taizu.
translations.idiomatic: The empress's mother was Emperor Taizu's younger sister.

sentences.zh: 睿宗為左副元帥，天會十三年薨，追封潞王，后封路遷妃。

translations.literal: Emperor Ruizong served as Left Deputy Commander-in-Chief; in the thirteenth year of Tianhui he died and was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Lu; the empress was created Princess of Lujian.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ruizong served as Left Deputy Commander-in-Chief. In the thirteenth year of Tianhui he died and was posthumously enfeoffed Prince of Lu; the empress was created Princess of Lujian.

sentences.zh: 皇統六年，進號冀國王妃。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Huangtong, she was advanced to Princess of Ji State.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Huangtong she was advanced to Princess of Ji State.

sentences.zh: 天德間，進國號。

translations.literal: During the Tiande era, she was advanced to the state title.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tiande era she received the full state title.

sentences.zh: 正隆例，親王止封一字王，睿宗封許王，后封許王妃。

translations.literal: By the precedent of Zhenglong, princes of the blood were enfeoffed with only a one-character princely title; Emperor Ruizong was enfeoffed as Prince of Xu, and the empress as Princess of Xu.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Zhenglong precedent, imperial princes received only a one-character princely title; Emperor Ruizong was enfeoffed Prince of Xu, and the empress Princess of Xu.

sentences.zh: 世宗即位，睿宗升祔，追諡欽慈皇后。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shizong took the throne, Emperor Ruizong was elevated to joint worship in the ancestral temple and posthumously titled Empress Qinci.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shizong ascended the throne, Emperor Ruizong was enshrined in the ancestral temple and the empress was posthumously titled Empress Qinci.

sentences.zh: 贈后曾祖賽補司空、韓國公，祖蒲刺司徒、鄭國公，父按補太尉、曹國公。

translations.literal: Her great-grandfather Saibu was posthumously enfeoffed as Minister of Works and Duke of Han State; her grandfather Puci as Minister of Education and Duke of Zheng State; her father Anbu as Grand Marshal and Duke of Cao State.
translations.idiomatic: Her great-grandfather Saibu was posthumously enfeoffed Minister of Works and Duke of Han; her grandfather Puci Minister of Education and Duke of Zheng; and her father Anbu Grand Marshal and Duke of Cao.

sentences.zh: 大定二年，祔葬景陵。

translations.literal: In the second year of Dading, she was buried jointly at Jingling.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Dading she was buried jointly at Jingling.

sentences.zh: 世宗嘗曰：「今之女直，不比前輩，雖親戚世敘，亦不能知其詳。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizong once said: "The Jurchen women of today are not like those of earlier generations; even when kinship is recorded generation by generation, one still cannot know the details.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizong once remarked, "Jurchen women today are not like those of earlier times—even when kinship is traced generation by generation, the particulars still cannot be known.

sentences.zh: 太后之母，太祖之妹，人亦不能知也。」

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager's mother was a younger sister of Emperor Taizu, yet people could not know this either."
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager's mother was Emperor Taizu's younger sister, and even that was unknown to most."

sentences.zh: 謂宗敘曰：「亦是卿父譚王之妹，知之乎？」

translations.literal: He said to Zongxu: "She was also a younger sister of your father Prince Tan—do you know this?"
translations.idiomatic: He asked Zongxu, "She was also your father Prince Tan's younger sister—did you know?"

sentences.zh: 宗敘曰：「臣不能知也。」

translations.literal: Zongxu said: "Your subject did not know."
translations.idiomatic: Zongxu replied, "I did not know, Your Majesty."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「父之妹且不知，其如疏遠何」。

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "If one does not even know one's father's younger sister, what of those more distantly related?"
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said, "If you do not even know your father's younger sister, what hope is there for more distant kin?"

sentences.zh: 十九年，后族人勸農使莎魯窩請致仕，宰相以莎魯窩未嘗曆外，請除一外官，以均勞佚。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year, Shaluguo of the empress's clan, Commissioner for Encouraging Agriculture, requested retirement. The chief ministers, noting that Shaluguo had never served outside the capital, asked that he be given an outside post to balance labor and rest.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year of his reign, Shaluguo of the empress's clan, who held the post of Commissioner for Encouraging Agriculture, asked to retire. The chief ministers observed that he had never served outside the capital and proposed appointing him to an outside office so that duties and leisure might be fairly distributed.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「莎魯窩不閑政事，不可使治民。

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "Shaluguo is unskilled in government affairs and must not be put in charge of the people.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said, "Shaluguo is unversed in statecraft and must not be entrusted with governing the people.

sentences.zh: 雖太后戚屬，富貴之可也。」

translations.literal: Though he is a kinsman of the Empress Dowager, it is enough that he enjoy wealth and honor."
translations.idiomatic: Though he is kin to the Empress Dowager, it is enough that he enjoy wealth and rank."

sentences.zh: 不聽。

translations.literal: He did not approve.
translations.idiomatic: He would not hear of it.

sentences.zh: 睿宗貞懿皇后

translations.literal: Empress Zhenyi of Emperor Ruizong
translations.idiomatic: Empress Zhenyi of Emperor Ruizong

sentences.zh: 貞懿皇后，李氏，世宗母，遼陽人。

translations.literal: Empress Zhenyi, surname Li, mother of Emperor Shizong, a native of Liaoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Zhenyi, née Li, was Emperor Shizong's mother and a native of Liaoyang.

sentences.zh: 父雛訛只，仕遼，官至桂州觀察使。

translations.literal: Her father Chuezhi served the Liao and rose to the post of Military Commissioner of Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Her father Chuezhi had served the Liao dynasty and risen to Military Commissioner of Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 天輔間，選東京士族女子有姿德者赴上京，后入睿宗邸。

translations.literal: During the Tianfu era, women of good family in the Eastern Capital who possessed beauty and virtue were selected and sent to the Supreme Capital; the empress entered the residence of Emperor Ruizong.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tianfu era, women of good birth in the Eastern Capital who possessed both beauty and virtue were chosen and sent to the Supreme Capital; she entered the household of Emperor Ruizong.

sentences.zh: 七年，世宗生。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, Emperor Shizong was born.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year she bore Emperor Shizong.

sentences.zh: 天會十三年，睿宗薨，世宗時年十三。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Tianhui, Emperor Ruizong died; Emperor Shizong was then thirteen.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year of Tianhui, Emperor Ruizong died; Emperor Shizong was then thirteen years old.

sentences.zh: 后教之有義方，嘗密謂所親曰：「吾兒有奇相，貴不可言。」

translations.literal: The empress taught him with proper principles and once said in secret to those close to her: "My son has an extraordinary countenance; his nobility cannot be put into words."
translations.idiomatic: The empress raised him with sound principles and once confided to those close to her, "My son bears an extraordinary countenance—his destiny is beyond words."

sentences.zh: 居上京，內治謹嚴，臧獲皆守規矩，衣服飲食器皿無不精潔，敦睦親族，周給貧乏，宗室中甚敬之。

translations.literal: Residing in the Supreme Capital, she governed the inner household with strict care; servants all observed rules; clothing, food, drink, and utensils were without exception refined and clean; she was warm to kin and gave generously to the poor; within the imperial clan she was greatly respected.
translations.idiomatic: While living in the Supreme Capital she ran the inner household with strict discipline; every servant observed the rules; clothing, food, drink, and utensils were kept immaculate; she was dutiful toward kin and generous to the needy; and the imperial clan held her in the highest regard.

sentences.zh: 后性明敏，剛正有決，容貌端整，言不妄發。

translations.literal: The empress was by nature clear-witted, upright and resolute, of dignified appearance, and did not speak rashly.
translations.idiomatic: She was quick-witted, upright, and decisive, with a composed bearing and a tongue that never spoke lightly.

sentences.zh: 舊俗，婦女寡居，宗族接續之。

translations.literal: By old custom, when a woman was widowed, the clan would take her in succession.
translations.idiomatic: By old custom, when a woman was widowed the clan would take her in levirate marriage.

sentences.zh: 后乃祝發為比丘尼，號通慧圓明大師，賜紫衣，歸遼陽，營建清安禪寺，別為尼院居之。

translations.literal: The empress thereupon tonsured her hair and became a bhikṣuṇī, styled Great Master Tonghui Yuanming, was granted purple robes, returned to Liaoyang, built Qing'an Chan Monastery, and had a separate nunnery erected for her residence.
translations.idiomatic: The empress instead tonsured her hair and became a Buddhist nun, taking the religious name Great Master Tonghui Yuanming; she was granted purple robes, returned to Liaoyang, founded Qing'an Chan Monastery, and had a separate nunnery built for her residence.

sentences.zh: 貞元三年，世宗為東京留守。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhenyuan, Emperor Shizong became Military Governor of the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Zhenyuan, Emperor Shizong was appointed Military Governor of the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 正隆六年五月，后卒。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the sixth year of Zhenglong, the empress died.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the sixth year of Zhenglong she died.

sentences.zh: 世宗哀毀過禮，以喪去官。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizong's grief exceeded ritual propriety, and he resigned his office on account of mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizong's grief exceeded what ritual prescribed, and he resigned his post to observe mourning.

sentences.zh: 未幾，起複為留守。

translations.literal: Before long he was recalled from mourning to resume the post of Military Governor.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was recalled from mourning and reappointed Military Governor.

sentences.zh: 是歲十月，后弟李石定策，世宗即位于東京，尊諡為貞懿皇后，其寢園曰孝甯宮。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of that year, the empress's younger brother Li Shi settled the strategy; Emperor Shizong took the throne in the Eastern Capital and honored her with the posthumous title Empress Zhenyi; her resting place was called Xiaoning Palace.
translations.idiomatic: That October her younger brother Li Shi masterminded the coup; Emperor Shizong ascended the throne in the Eastern Capital, posthumously honored her as Empress Zhenyi, and named her resting place Xiaoning Palace.

sentences.zh: 大定二年，改葬睿宗于景陵。

translations.literal: In the second year of Dading, Emperor Ruizong was reinterred at Jingling.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Dading, Emperor Ruizong was reinterred at Jingling.

sentences.zh: 初，后自建浮圖于遼陽，是為垂慶寺，臨終謂世宗曰：「鄉土之念，人情所同，吾已用浮屠法置塔於此，不必合葬也。

translations.literal: Earlier the empress had herself built a stūpa at Liaoyang, which became Chuaiqing Monastery. On her deathbed she told Emperor Shizong: "Longing for one's native place is what all feel alike; I have already used the Buddhist method to place a tower here—there is no need for joint burial.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier she had built a stūpa at Liaoyang, which became Chuaiqing Monastery. On her deathbed she told Emperor Shizong, "Longing for one's homeland is universal; I have already raised a tower here by Buddhist rite—there is no need for us to be buried together.

sentences.zh: 我死，毋忘此言。」

translations.literal: When I die, do not forget these words."
translations.idiomatic: When I am gone, do not forget what I have said."

sentences.zh: 世宗深念遺命，乃即東京清安寺建神禦殿，詔有司增大舊塔，起奉茲殿於塔前。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizong deeply kept her last command in mind; thereupon at Qing'an Monastery in the Eastern Capital he built a Spirit Tablet Hall, ordered the officials to enlarge the old tower, and erected this hall for worship before the tower.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizong held her last wish close at heart. At Qing'an Monastery in the Eastern Capital he built a Spirit Tablet Hall, ordered officials to enlarge the old tower, and raised the hall for worship before it.

sentences.zh: 敕禮部尚書王競為塔銘以敘其意。

translations.literal: He commanded Minister of Rites Wang Jing to compose an inscription for the tower setting forth her intent.
translations.idiomatic: He charged Minister of Rites Wang Jing with composing a tower inscription to record her intent.

sentences.zh: 贈后曾祖參君司空、潞國公，祖波司徒、衛國公，父雛訛只太尉、隋國公。

translations.literal: He posthumously ennobled the empress's great-grandfather Canjun as Grand Preceptor and Duke of Lu, her grandfather Bo as Minister of Education and Duke of Wei, and her father Chuezhi as Grand Marshal and Duke of Sui.
translations.idiomatic: He posthumously ennobled her great-grandfather Canjun as Grand Preceptor and Duke of Lu, her grandfather Bo as Minister of Education and Duke of Wei, and her father Chuezhi as Grand Marshal and Duke of Sui.

sentences.zh: 四年，封后妹為邢國夫人，賜銀千兩、錦綺二十端、絹五百匹。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, he enfeoffed the empress's younger sister as Lady of Xing State and bestowed one thousand taels of silver, twenty bolts of brocade silk, and five hundred bolts of plain silk.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he enfeoffed her younger sister as Lady of Xing State and bestowed one thousand taels of silver, twenty bolts of brocade silk, and five hundred bolts of plain silk.

sentences.zh: 九年，神禦殿名曰報德殿。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, the Spirit Tablet Hall was named Hall of Repaying Virtue.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year the Spirit Tablet Hall was named the Hall of Repaying Virtue.

sentences.zh: 詔翰林學士張景仁作《清安寺碑》，其文不稱旨，詔左丞石琚共修之。

translations.literal: He ordered Academician Zhang Jingren to compose the "Stele of Qing'an Monastery"; the text did not please him, and he commanded Left Vice Censor-in-Chief Shi Ju to revise it jointly.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Academician Zhang Jingren to compose the Stele of Qing'an Monastery; when the draft did not please him, he charged Left Vice Censor-in-Chief Shi Ju to revise it jointly.

sentences.zh: 十三年，東京垂慶寺起神禦殿，寺地褊狹，詔賈傍近民地，優與其直，不願鬻者以官地易之。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, at Chuaiqing Monastery in the Eastern Capital a Spirit Tablet Hall was raised; the monastery grounds were cramped, and an edict ordered the purchase of neighboring private land at favorable prices; those unwilling to sell were given official land in exchange.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year a Spirit Tablet Hall was raised at Chuaiqing Monastery in the Eastern Capital; the grounds were cramped, so an edict ordered the purchase of neighboring private land at favorable prices, and those unwilling to sell were given official land in exchange.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，世宗至東京，幸清安、垂慶寺。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year, Emperor Shizong came to the Eastern Capital and visited Qing'an and Chuaiqing monasteries.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fourth year Emperor Shizong traveled to the Eastern Capital and visited Qing'an and Chuaiqing monasteries.

sentences.zh: 世宗昭德皇后

translations.literal: Empress Zhaode of Emperor Shizong
translations.idiomatic: Empress Zhaode of Emperor Shizong

sentences.zh: 烏林荅氏，其先居羅伊河，世為烏林荅部長，率部族來歸，居上京，與本朝為婚姻家。

translations.literal: Of the Wulindá clan; their forebears dwelt on the Luoyi River and for generations were chiefs of the Wulindá tribe; they led their clansmen to submit, settled in the Supreme Capital, and became a marriage-alliance house with the dynasty.
translations.idiomatic: She was of the Wulindá clan. Her ancestors had lived on the Luoyi River and for generations had been chiefs of the Wulindá tribe; they led their people to submit, settled in the Supreme Capital, and became a marriage-alliance kin of the dynasty.

sentences.zh: 曾祖勝管，康宗時累使高麗。

translations.literal: Her great-grandfather Shengguan, during the time of Emperor Kang, was repeatedly sent as envoy to Goryeo.
translations.idiomatic: Her great-grandfather Shengguan had served repeatedly as envoy to Goryeo under Emperor Kang.

sentences.zh: 父石土黑，騎射絕倫，從太祖伐遼，領行軍猛安。

translations.literal: Her father Shituhei was without peer in horsemanship and archery, followed Emperor Taizu in the campaign against Liao, and commanded a field meng'an.
translations.idiomatic: Her father Shituhei was unrivaled in horsemanship and archery; he followed Emperor Taizu against the Liao and commanded a field meng'an.

sentences.zh: 雖在行伍間，不嗜殺人。

translations.literal: Though among the ranks of soldiers, he did not delight in killing men.
translations.idiomatic: Even amid the ranks of war he took no pleasure in killing.

sentences.zh: 以功授世襲謀克，為東京留守。

translations.literal: For merit he was granted a hereditary meng'an and became Military Governor of the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: For his merit he was granted a hereditary meng'an and appointed Military Governor of the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 后聰敏孝慈，容儀整肅，在父母家，宗族皆敬重之。

translations.literal: The empress was intelligent, filial, and compassionate, of dignified bearing; in her parents' house the whole clan respected her.
translations.idiomatic: The empress was quick-witted, filial, and compassionate, with a composed bearing; in her parents' household the entire clan held her in esteem.

sentences.zh: 既歸世宗，事舅姑孝謹，治家有敘，甚得婦道。

translations.literal: After she married Emperor Shizong, she served her parents-in-law with filial care, kept the household in order, and fully embodied the way of a wife.
translations.idiomatic: After she married Emperor Shizong she served her parents-in-law with filial devotion, kept the household in good order, and fully embodied the duties of a wife.

sentences.zh: 睿宗伐宋，得白玉帶，蓋帝王之服禦也。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ruizong campaigned against Song, he obtained a white jade belt—the kind of regalia proper to an emperor.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ruizong campaigned against Song he captured a white jade belt—the sort of regalia reserved for emperors.

sentences.zh: 睿宗沒後，世宗寶畜之。

translations.literal: After Emperor Ruizong's death, Emperor Shizong treasured and kept it.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Ruizong's death, Emperor Shizong kept it as a treasured heirloom.

sentences.zh: 后謂世宗曰：「此非王邸所宜有也，當獻之天子。」

translations.literal: The empress said to Emperor Shizong: "This is not what a princely residence ought to possess; it should be presented to the Son of Heaven."
translations.idiomatic: The empress told Emperor Shizong, "A princely household ought not keep such a thing—it should be presented to the Son of Heaven."

sentences.zh: 世宗以為然，獻之熙宗，於是悼后大喜。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizong thought this right and presented it to Emperor Xizong; thereupon Empress Dao was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizong agreed and presented it to Emperor Xizong, and Empress Dao was greatly pleased.

sentences.zh: 熙宗晚年頗酗酒，獨于世宗無間然。

translations.literal: In his later years Emperor Xizong drank heavily, yet toward Emperor Shizong alone he was without estrangement.
translations.idiomatic: In his later years Emperor Xizong drank heavily, yet toward Emperor Shizong alone he showed no estrangement.

sentences.zh: 海陵篡立，深忌宗室。

translations.literal: When Emperor Hailing usurped the throne, he deeply feared the imperial clan.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Hailing seized the throne he deeply feared the imperial clan.

sentences.zh: 烏帶譖秉德以為意在葛王。

translations.literal: Wudai slandered Bingde, alleging that his intent lay with Prince Ge.
translations.idiomatic: Wudai slandered Bingde, alleging that his loyalty lay with Prince Ge.

sentences.zh: 秉德誅死，后勸世宗多獻珍異以說其心，如故遼骨睹犀佩刀、吐鶻良玉茶器之類，皆奇寶也。

translations.literal: Bingde was executed; the empress urged Emperor Shizong to present many rare treasures to win his heart—such as the old Liao bone-tu rhinoceros-horn belt knife, touhu fine jade tea vessels, and the like, all wondrous treasures.
translations.idiomatic: Bingde was executed. The empress urged Emperor Shizong to win Hailing over with rare gifts—the old Liao bone-tu rhinoceros-horn belt knife, touhu fine-jade tea vessels, and the like, all extraordinary treasures.

sentences.zh: 海陵以世宗恭順畏己，由是忌刻之心頗解。

translations.literal: Emperor Hailing, seeing Emperor Shizong respectful and in awe of him, thereby somewhat relaxed his jealous suspicion.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing Emperor Shizong respectful and fearful of him, Hailing's jealous suspicion eased somewhat.

sentences.zh: 后不妒忌，為世宗擇后房，廣繼嗣，雖顯宗生後而此心不移。

translations.literal: The empress was free of jealousy; she selected consorts for Emperor Shizong to broaden the succession; even after Emperor Xianzong was born this purpose did not change.
translations.idiomatic: The empress was free of jealousy; she chose consorts for Emperor Shizong to broaden the line of succession, and even after Emperor Xianzong was born her purpose did not waver.

sentences.zh: 后嘗有疾，世宗為視醫藥，數日不離去。

translations.literal: When the empress once fell ill, Emperor Shizong personally attended to her medicine and for several days did not leave her side.
translations.idiomatic: When she once fell ill, Emperor Shizong personally saw to her medicine and for several days did not leave her side.

sentences.zh: 后曰：「大王視妾過厚，其知者以為視疾，不知者必有專妒之嫌。」

translations.literal: The empress said: "Your Highness shows your handmaid too much favor; those who know will take it as nursing an illness, but those who do not will surely suspect exclusive jealousy."
translations.idiomatic: The empress said, "Your Highness shows me too much favor; those who understand will call it nursing an illness, but those who do not will suspect possessive jealousy."

sentences.zh: 又曰：「婦道以正家為大，第恐德薄，無補內治，安能效嬪妾所為，惟欲己厚也。」

translations.literal: She also said: "The way of a wife takes setting the household right as paramount; I only fear my virtue is slight and of no help to inner governance—how could I imitate what concubines do, seeking only my own advantage?"
translations.idiomatic: She added, "A wife's duty is above all to set the household right; I only fear my virtue is too slight to aid inner governance—how could I imitate what concubines do and seek only my own advantage?"

sentences.zh: 世宗在濟南，海陵召后來中都。

translations.literal: While Emperor Shizong was in Jinan, Emperor Hailing summoned the empress to the Central Capital.
translations.idiomatic: While Emperor Shizong was in Jinan, Emperor Hailing summoned the empress to the Central Capital.

sentences.zh: 后念若身死濟南，海陵必殺世宗，惟奉詔，去濟南而死，世宗可以免。

translations.literal: The empress reflected that if she died in Jinan, Emperor Hailing would surely kill Emperor Shizong; only by obeying the summons, leaving Jinan and dying elsewhere, could Emperor Shizong be spared.
translations.idiomatic: The empress reasoned that if she died in Jinan, Hailing would surely kill Emperor Shizong; only by obeying the summons, leaving Jinan, and dying elsewhere could her husband be spared.

sentences.zh: 謂世宗曰：「我當自勉，不可累大王也。」

translations.literal: She told Emperor Shizong: "I shall strive on my own and must not implicate Your Highness."
translations.idiomatic: She told Emperor Shizong, "I shall do my utmost on my own and must not bring trouble upon you."

sentences.zh: 召王府臣僕張僅言諭之曰：「汝，王之腹心人也。

translations.literal: She summoned the prince's servant Zhang Jinyan and instructed him: "You are the prince's trusted man.
translations.idiomatic: She summoned the prince's retainer Zhang Jinyan and told him, "You are the prince's trusted man.

sentences.zh: 為我禱諸東嶽，我不負王，使皇天后土明鑒我心。」

translations.literal: Pray for me at Mount Tai; I have not failed the prince—let Heaven and Earth clearly witness my heart."
translations.idiomatic: Pray for me at Mount Tai. I have not failed the prince—let Heaven and Earth bear witness to my heart."

sentences.zh: 召家人謂之曰：「我自初年為婦以至今日，未嘗見王有違道之事。

translations.literal: She summoned the household and told them: "From the year I first became a wife until today, I have never seen the prince do anything contrary to the Way.
translations.idiomatic: She gathered the household and said, "From the day I became his wife until now, I have never seen the prince do anything unworthy.

sentences.zh: 今宗室往往被疑者，皆奴僕不良，傲恨其主，以誣陷之耳。

translations.literal: Those of the imperial clan who are now so often suspected are all victims of bad servants who, proud and resentful toward their masters, slander and entrap them.
translations.idiomatic: Those of the imperial clan who are now so often suspected are victims of wicked servants who, proud and resentful toward their masters, slander and entrap them.

sentences.zh: 汝等皆先國王時舊人，當念舊恩，無或妄圖也。

translations.literal: You are all old retainers from the time of the former prince; you should remember old kindness and must not harbor reckless designs.
translations.idiomatic: You are all old retainers from the former prince's household; remember his kindness and harbor no reckless designs.

sentences.zh: 違此言者，我死後於冥中觀汝所為。」

translations.literal: Whoever violates these words—after my death in the nether world I shall watch what you do."
translations.idiomatic: Whoever violates these words—after my death I shall watch what you do from the nether world."

sentences.zh: 眾皆泣下。

translations.literal: All wept.
translations.idiomatic: All wept.

sentences.zh: 后既離濟南，從行者知后必不肯見海陵，將自為之所，防護甚謹。

translations.literal: After the empress left Jinan, those accompanying her knew she would surely refuse to see Emperor Hailing and would take matters into her own hands; they guarded her very strictly.
translations.idiomatic: After she left Jinan, her escorts knew she would never submit to Hailing and would take her own course; they guarded her very strictly.

sentences.zh: 行至良鄉，去中都七十裏，從行者防之稍緩，后得間即自殺。

translations.literal: When they reached Liangxiang, seventy li from the Central Capital, the escorts' vigilance slackened somewhat; the empress seized the opportunity and at once took her own life.
translations.idiomatic: At Liangxiang, seventy li from the Central Capital, the escorts' vigilance slackened; she seized the moment and took her own life.

sentences.zh: 海陵猶疑世宗教之使然。

translations.literal: Emperor Hailing still suspected that Emperor Shizong had taught her to do this.
translations.idiomatic: Hailing still suspected that Emperor Shizong had instructed her to do it.

sentences.zh: 世宗自濟南改西京留守，過良鄉，使魯國公主葬后於宛平縣土魯原。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shizong was transferred from Jinan to Military Governor of the Western Capital and passed Liangxiang, he had the Princess of Lu State bury the empress at Tulu Plain in Wanping County.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shizong was transferred from Jinan to Military Governor of the Western Capital and passed Liangxiang, he had the Princess of Lu State bury the empress at Tulu Plain in Wanping County.

sentences.zh: 大定二年，追冊為昭德皇后，立別廟。

translations.literal: In the second year of Dading she was posthumously enfeoffed as Empress Zhaode and a separate temple was established.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Dading she was posthumously enfeoffed as Empress Zhaode and given a separate ancestral temple.

sentences.zh: 贈三代，曾祖勝管司空、徐國公，曾祖母完顏氏徐國夫人，祖術思黑司徒、代國公，祖母完顏氏，代國夫人，父石土黑太尉、瀋國公，母完顏氏瀋國夫人。

translations.literal: Three generations were ennobled: great-grandfather Shengguan as Grand Preceptor and Duke of Xu, great-grandmother née Wanyan as Lady of Xu State, grandfather Shusihei as Minister of Education and Duke of Dai, grandmother née Wanyan as Lady of Dai State, father Shituhei as Grand Marshal and Duke of Shen, mother née Wanyan as Lady of Shen State.
translations.idiomatic: Three generations were ennobled: her great-grandfather Shengguan as Grand Preceptor and Duke of Xu, her great-grandmother née Wanyan as Lady of Xu State, her grandfather Shusihei as Minister of Education and Duke of Dai, her grandmother née Wanyan as Lady of Dai State, her father Shituhei as Grand Marshal and Duke of Shen, and her mother née Wanyan as Lady of Shen State.

sentences.zh: 敕有司改葬，命皇太子致奠。

translations.literal: He commanded the officials to reinter her and ordered the Crown Prince to offer libations.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered officials to reinter her and commanded the Crown Prince to offer libations.

sentences.zh: 以后兄暉子天錫為太尉，石土黑後授世襲猛安。

translations.literal: He made the empress's elder brother's son Hui's son Tiansi Grand Marshal; after Shituhei, the hereditary meng'an was granted.
translations.idiomatic: He appointed the empress's nephew Tiansi, son of her elder brother's son Hui, as Grand Marshal; after Shituhei the hereditary meng'an passed to his heirs.

sentences.zh: 上謂天錫曰：「朕四五歲時與皇后訂婚，乃祖太尉置朕于膝上曰：'吾婿七人，此婿最幼，後來必大吾門。

translations.literal: The Emperor said to Tiansi: "When I was four or five years old I was betrothed to the empress; her grandfather the Grand Marshal set me on his knee and said: 'I have seven sons-in-law; this son-in-law is the youngest—later he will surely enlarge my house.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor told Tiansi, "When I was four or five I was betrothed to the empress. Her grandfather the Grand Marshal set me on his knee and said, 'I have seven sons-in-law; this one is the youngest—later he will surely enlarge my house.

sentences.zh: '今卜葬有期，疇昔之言驗矣。」

translations.literal: Now that the date of burial is fixed, words of long ago are fulfilled.'"
translations.idiomatic: Now that her burial is at hand, his words of long ago have come true.'"

sentences.zh: 六年，利涉軍節度副使烏林荅鈔兀捕逃軍受贓，當殆。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, Wulindá Chaowu, Vice Military Commissioner of Lishes Army, in capturing deserters accepted bribes and was liable to death.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year, Wulindá Chaowu, Vice Military Commissioner of Lishes Army, accepted bribes while capturing deserters and faced the death penalty.

sentences.zh: 有司奏，鈔兀，后大功親，當議。

translations.literal: The officials memorialized that Chaowu was a relative of the empress within the degree of dagong and the case should be deliberated.
translations.idiomatic: Officials memorialized that Chaowu was a relative of the empress within the degree of dagong and that the case warranted deliberation.

sentences.zh: 詔論如法。

translations.literal: An edict ordered judgment according to law.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered that he be judged according to law.

sentences.zh: 八年七月，章宗上，世宗喜甚。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the eighth year, Zhangzong was born; Emperor Shizong was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the eighth year Zhangzong was born, and Emperor Shizong was overjoyed.

sentences.zh: 謂顯宗曰：「得社稷塚嗣，朕樂何極。

translations.literal: He said to Emperor Xianzong: "To obtain the heir of the altars of state—how could my joy be greater?
translations.idiomatic: He told Emperor Xianzong, "To have secured the heir of the altars of state—my joy knows no bounds.

sentences.zh: 此皇后貽爾以陰德也。」

translations.literal: This is the hidden virtue the empress bequeathed to you."
translations.idiomatic: This is the hidden virtue the empress bequeathed to you."

sentences.zh: 十年十月，將改葬太尉石土黑，有司奏禮儀，援唐葬太尉李良器、司徒馬燧故事，百官便服送至都門外五裏。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the tenth year, when Grand Marshal Shituhei was to be reinterred, the officials memorialized on ritual, citing Tang precedents for the burial of Grand Marshal Li Liangqi and Minister of Education Ma Sui: all officials in ordinary dress escorted the coffin five li beyond the capital gate.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of the tenth year, as Grand Marshal Shituhei was to be reinterred, officials memorialized on ritual, citing Tang precedents for the burials of Grand Marshal Li Liangqi and Minister of Education Ma Sui: all officials in ordinary dress were to escort the coffin five li beyond the capital gate.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「前改葬太后父母，未嘗用此故事。

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "When the Empress Dowager's parents were reinterred earlier, this precedent was never used.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said, "When the Empress Dowager's parents were reinterred earlier, this precedent was not followed.

sentences.zh: 但以本朝禮改葬之，惟親戚皆送。」

translations.literal: Only follow this dynasty's rites for reburial; let kin alone escort."
translations.idiomatic: Follow only our dynasty's rites for reburial; let kin alone escort the coffin."

sentences.zh: 詔皇太子臨奠。

translations.literal: He ordered the Crown Prince to offer libations on site.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered the Crown Prince to offer libations on site.

sentences.zh: 十一年，皇太子生日，世宗宴於東宮。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, on the Crown Prince's birthday, Emperor Shizong feasted at the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year, on the Crown Prince's birthday, Emperor Shizong held a feast at the Eastern Palace.

sentences.zh: 酒酣，命豫國公主起舞。

translations.literal: When the wine had warmed them, he commanded the Princess of Yu State to dance.
translations.idiomatic: When the wine had warmed them, he commanded the Princess of Yu State to dance.

sentences.zh: 上流涕曰：「此女之母皇后，婦道至矣。

translations.literal: The Emperor, weeping, said: "This girl's mother the empress embodied the way of a wife to the utmost.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor wept and said, "This girl's mother the empress embodied the duties of a wife to the utmost.

sentences.zh: 朕所以不立中宮者，念皇后之德今無其比故也。」

translations.literal: The reason I have not established a Central Palace is that I reflect on the empress's virtue—for now there is none to compare with her."
translations.idiomatic: The reason I have not installed a new empress is that I reflect on her virtue—for now there is none to compare with her."

sentences.zh: 十二年四月，立皇后別廟于太廟東北隅。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the twelfth year, a separate temple for the empress was established at the northeast corner of the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the twelfth year a separate temple for the empress was established at the northeast corner of the Imperial Ancestral Temple.

sentences.zh: 是歲五月，車駕幸士魯原致奠。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of that year, the imperial carriage visited Tulu Plain to offer libations.
translations.idiomatic: That May the imperial carriage visited Tulu Plain to offer libations.

sentences.zh: 十九年，改卜於大房山。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year, the burial site was changed to Mount Dafang.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year the burial site was moved to Mount Dafang.

sentences.zh: 十一月甲寅，皇后梓宮至近郊，百官奉迎。

translations.literal: On jiayin day of the eleventh month, the empress's coffin reached the suburbs; all officials came forth to welcome it.
translations.idiomatic: On jiayin day of the eleventh month the empress's coffin reached the suburbs, and all officials came forth to welcome it.

sentences.zh: 乙卯，車駕如楊村致祭。

translations.literal: On yimao day, the imperial carriage went to Yang Village to offer sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: On yimao day the imperial carriage went to Yang Village to offer sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 丙辰，上登車送，哭之慟。

translations.literal: On bingchen day, the Emperor mounted his carriage to escort her and wept with deep grief.
translations.idiomatic: On bingchen day the Emperor mounted his carriage to escort her and wept with deep grief.

sentences.zh: 戊午，奉安于磐甯宮。

translations.literal: On wuwu day, she was installed for repose at Panning Palace.
translations.idiomatic: On wuwu day she was installed for repose at Panning Palace.

sentences.zh: 庚申，葬於坤厚陵，諸妃祔焉。

translations.literal: On gengshen day, she was buried at Kunhou Mausoleum; all consorts were enshrined there with her.
translations.idiomatic: On gengshen day she was buried at Kunhou Mausoleum, with all consorts enshrined there beside her.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，祔葬興陵。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year, she was jointly buried at Xingling.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-ninth year she was jointly buried at Xingling.

sentences.zh: 章宗時，有司奏太祖諡有「昭德」字，改諡明德皇后。

translations.literal: During the time of Emperor Zhangzong, the officials memorialized that Emperor Taizu's posthumous title contained the character "Zhaode," and her title was changed to Empress Mingde.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Zhangzong, officials memorialized that Emperor Taizu's posthumous title contained the character "Zhaode," and her title was changed to Empress Mingde.

sentences.zh: 世宗元妃張氏

translations.literal: First Consort Zhang of Emperor Shizong
translations.idiomatic: First Consort Zhang of Emperor Shizong

sentences.zh: 元妃張氏，父玄征。

translations.literal: First Consort Zhang; her father was Xuanzheng.
translations.idiomatic: First Consort Zhang; her father was Xuanzheng.

sentences.zh: 母高氏，與世宗母貞懿皇后葭莩親。

translations.literal: Her mother was of the Gao clan, a marriage-alliance kin of Emperor Shizong's mother Empress Zhenyi.
translations.idiomatic: Her mother was of the Gao clan, related by marriage to Emperor Shizong's mother Empress Zhenyi.

sentences.zh: 世宗納為次室，生趙王永中，而張氏卒。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizong took her as secondary consort; she bore Prince Zhao Yongzhong, and then Zhang died.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizong took her as secondary consort; she bore Prince Zhao Yongzhong, then died.

sentences.zh: 大定二年，追封宸妃。

translations.literal: In the second year of Dading she was posthumously enfeoffed as Noble Consort.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Dading she was posthumously enfeoffed as Noble Consort.

sentences.zh: 是歲十月，追進惠妃。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of that year she was further advanced to Kind Consort.
translations.idiomatic: That October she was further advanced to Kind Consort.

sentences.zh: 十九年，追進元妃。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year she was further advanced to First Consort.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year she was further advanced to First Consort.

sentences.zh: 大定二十五年，皇太子薨。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year of Dading, the Crown Prince died.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fifth year of Dading the Crown Prince died.

sentences.zh: 永中于諸子最長，而世宗與徒單克甯議立章宗為太孫。

translations.literal: Yongzhong was eldest among the sons, yet Emperor Shizong and Tudan Kening deliberated establishing Zhangzong as Imperial Grandson.
translations.idiomatic: Yongzhong was the eldest son, yet Emperor Shizong and Tudan Kening decided to establish Zhangzong as Imperial Grandson.

sentences.zh: 世宗嘗曰：「克寧與永中有親，而建議立太孫，真社會稷臣也。」

translations.literal: Emperor Shizong once said: "Kening is kin to Yongzhong, yet he proposed establishing the Imperial Grandson—a true minister of altars and state."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizong once said, "Kening is kin to Yongzhong, yet he proposed establishing the Imperial Grandson—a true minister of altars and state."

sentences.zh: 尚書左丞汝弼者，玄征子，永中每舅。

translations.literal: Left Vice Minister of the Secretariat Rubi was Xuanzheng's son and Yongzhong's maternal uncle.
translations.idiomatic: Left Vice Minister Rubi was Xuanzheng's son and Yongzhong's maternal uncle.

sentences.zh: 汝弼妻高陀斡屢以邪言怵永中，畫元妃像，朝夕事之，覬望徼福，及挾左道。

translations.literal: Rubi's wife Gaotuowo repeatedly alarmed Yongzhong with heterodox words, painted an image of the First Consort and served it morning and evening, hoping to gain blessing by chance, and moreover practiced sorcery.
translations.idiomatic: Rubi's wife Gaotuowo repeatedly alarmed Yongzhong with heterodox talk, painted an image of the First Consort and worshipped it morning and evening in hope of blessing, and practiced sorcery as well.

sentences.zh: 明昌五年，高陀斡誅死，事連汝弼及永中，汝弼以死後事覺，得不追削官爵，而章宗心疑永中，累年不釋。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Mingchang, Gaotuowo was executed; the affair implicated Rubi and Yongzhong. Because Rubi's crimes came to light only after his death, his titles were not posthumously stripped, but Emperor Zhangzong harbored suspicion of Yongzhong for many years without release.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Mingchang Gaotuowo was executed; the affair implicated Rubi and Yongzhong. Because Rubi's crimes came to light only after his death, his titles were not posthumously stripped, but Emperor Zhangzong harbored suspicion of Yongzhong for many years.

sentences.zh: 諫官賈守謙、路鐸上疏欲寬解上意，章宗愈不悅。

translations.literal: Remonstrating officials Jia Shouqian and Lu Duo memorialized wishing to ease the Emperor's mind; Emperor Zhangzong was all the more displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Remonstrating officials Jia Shouqian and Lu Duo memorialized hoping to ease the Emperor's mind; Zhangzong was all the more displeased.

sentences.zh: 平章政事完顏守貞持其事不肯決，章宗怒守貞，罷知濟南府，諸諫官皆斥外，賜永中死。

translations.literal: Chief Councilor Wanyan Shouzhen held to the case and would not decide; Emperor Zhangzong was angry with Shouzhen, dismissed him to govern Jinan Prefecture, expelled all the remonstrators to outside posts, and granted Yongzhong death.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Councilor Wanyan Shouzhen refused to decide the case; Zhangzong was angry with him, dismissed him to govern Jinan Prefecture, expelled all the remonstrators to outside posts, and ordered Yongzhong to die.

sentences.zh: 金代外戚之禍，惟張氏雲。

translations.literal: Among the calamities of maternal kin in the Jin dynasty, only the Zhang clan is spoken of thus.
translations.idiomatic: Of the calamities wrought by maternal kin in the Jin dynasty, only the Zhang clan is spoken of in this way.

sentences.zh: 元妃李氏，南陽郡王李石女。

translations.literal: First Consort Li, daughter of Li Shi, Prince of Nanyang Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: First Consort Li was the daughter of Li Shi, Prince of Nanyang Commandery.

sentences.zh: 生鄭王允蹈、衛紹王允濟、潞王允德。

translations.literal: She bore Princes Yunchao of Zheng, Yunji of Wei, and Yunde of Lu.
translations.idiomatic: She bore Princes Yunchao of Zheng, Yunji of Wei, and Yunde of Lu.

sentences.zh: 豫王允成母昭儀梁氏早卒，上命允成為妃養子。

translations.literal: Prince Yuncheng's mother, Lady Liang the Zhaoyi, died early; the Emperor ordered Yuncheng to be adopted as the consort's son.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yuncheng's mother, Lady Liang the Zhaoyi, had died early, and the emperor ordered that Yuncheng be adopted as the consort's son.

sentences.zh: 大定元年，封賢妃。

translations.literal: In the first year of Dading, she was created Worthy Consort.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Dading she was created Worthy Consort.

sentences.zh: 二年，進封貴妃。

translations.literal: In the second year, she was advanced to Honored Consort.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year she was advanced to Honored Consort.

sentences.zh: 七年，進封元妃。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, she was advanced to First Consort.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year she was advanced to First Consort.

sentences.zh: 世宗即位，感念昭德皇后，不復立后。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shizong took the throne, mindful of Empress Zhaode, he did not again establish an empress.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shizong took the throne, mindful of Empress Zhaode, he did not establish a new empress.

sentences.zh: 嘗曰：「朕所以不復立后者，今後宮無皇后之賢故也。」

translations.literal: He once said: "The reason I do not again establish an empress is that there is now no one in the inner palace with the virtue of an empress."
translations.idiomatic: He once said, "The reason I do not establish a new empress is that no woman in the inner palace now possesses an empress's virtue."

sentences.zh: 元妃下皇后一等，在諸妃上。

translations.literal: The First Consort ranked one grade below the empress and above all other consorts.
translations.idiomatic: The First Consort ranked one grade below empress and above all other consorts.

sentences.zh: 石有定策功，世宗厚而深制之，寵以尚書令之位，而責成左右丞相以下，妃雖貴，不得預政，宮壺無事。

translations.literal: Li Shi had the merit of settling the succession; Emperor Shizong treated him generously yet restrained him deeply, honoring him with the post of Director of the Department of State Affairs while charging the left and right chief councilors and those below to keep watch; though the consort was exalted, she could not participate in government, and the inner palace was without incident.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shi had helped settle the succession; Emperor Shizong honored him yet kept him tightly restrained, granting him the post of Director of the Department of State Affairs while charging the chief councilors and their subordinates to keep watch. Though the consort was exalted, she could not participate in government, and the inner palace remained untroubled.

sentences.zh: 大定二十一年二月，上如春水，次長春宮。

translations.literal: In the second month of the twenty-first year of Dading, the Emperor went to the spring hunt and halted at Changchun Palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the twenty-first year of Dading the Emperor went to the spring hunt and halted at Changchun Palace.

sentences.zh: 戊子，妃以疾薨。

translations.literal: On wuzi day, the consort died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: On wuzi day the consort died of illness.

sentences.zh: 詔允成、允蹈、允濟、允德皆服衰絰居喪。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Yuncheng, Yunchao, Yunji, and Yunde all to wear hemp mourning and observe the funeral rites.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Yuncheng, Yunchao, Yunji, and Yunde all to wear hemp mourning and observe funeral rites.

sentences.zh: 己丑，皇太子及扈從臣僚，奉慰於芳明殿。

translations.literal: On jichou day, the Crown Prince and accompanying officials offered condolences at Fangming Hall.
translations.idiomatic: On jichou day the Crown Prince and accompanying officials offered condolences at Fangming Hall.

sentences.zh: 辛卯，留守官平章政事唐括安禮、曹王允功等上表奉慰。

translations.literal: On xinmao day, the officials left behind—Chief Councilor Tangguo Anli and Prince of Cao Yungong and others—submitted a memorial offering condolences.
translations.idiomatic: On xinmao day the officials left behind—Chief Councilor Tangguo Anli and Prince of Cao Yungong among others—submitted a memorial offering condolences.

sentences.zh: 禦史中丞張九思提控殯事，少府監左光慶、大興少尹王翛典領鹵簿儀仗。

translations.literal: Censor-in-Chief Zhang Jiusi supervised the funeral arrangements; Director of the Palace Storehouses Zuo Guangqing and Vice Magistrate of Daxing Wang Xiao directed the funeral escort and ceremonial regalia.
translations.idiomatic: Censor-in-Chief Zhang Jiusi supervised the funeral arrangements; Director of the Palace Storehouses Zuo Guangqing and Vice Magistrate of Daxing Wang Xiao directed the funeral escort and ceremonial regalia.

sentences.zh: 宮籍監別治殯所，還殯京師。

translations.literal: The Palace Registry Office separately prepared the funeral site and returned the coffin to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: The Palace Registry Office prepared a separate funeral site and returned the coffin to the capital.

sentences.zh: 乙未，入自崇智門，百官郊迎，親戚迎奠道路，殯于興德宮西位別室。

translations.literal: On yiwei day, entering by Chongzhi Gate, all officials welcomed her at the suburbs; kin offered libations along the road; the coffin lay in a separate chamber at the western wing of Xingde Palace.
translations.idiomatic: On yiwei day, entering by Chongzhi Gate, all officials welcomed her at the suburbs; kin offered libations along the road; the coffin lay in a separate chamber at the western wing of Xingde Palace.

sentences.zh: 庚子，上至京師，幸興德宮致奠。

translations.literal: On gengzi day, the Emperor reached the capital and visited Xingde Palace to offer libations.
translations.idiomatic: On gengzi day the Emperor reached the capital and visited Xingde Palace to offer libations.

sentences.zh: 此葬，三致尊焉。

translations.literal: For this burial, he three times showed utmost honor.
translations.idiomatic: For this burial he showed utmost honor three times.

sentences.zh: 詔平章政事烏古論元忠監護葬事。

translations.literal: He ordered Chief Councilor Wugulun Yuanzhong to supervise the burial.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Chief Councilor Wugulun Yuanzhong to supervise the burial.

sentences.zh: 癸未，啟取，上輟朝。

translations.literal: On guiwei day, when the coffin was opened for removal, the Emperor suspended court.
translations.idiomatic: On guiwei day, when the coffin was opened for removal, the Emperor suspended court.

sentences.zh: 皇太子、親王、宗戚、百官送葬。

translations.literal: The Crown Prince, imperial princes, clan kin, and all officials escorted the burial.
translations.idiomatic: The Crown Prince, imperial princes, clan kin, and all officials escorted the burial.

sentences.zh: 甲申，葬于海王莊。

translations.literal: On jiashen day, she was buried at Haiwang Manor.
translations.idiomatic: On jiashen day she was buried at Haiwang Manor.

sentences.zh: 丙戌，上如海王莊燒飯。

translations.literal: On bingxu day, the Emperor went to Haiwang Manor to offer burnt food.
translations.idiomatic: On bingxu day the Emperor went to Haiwang Manor to offer burnt food at the grave.

sentences.zh: 二十八年九月，與賢妃石抹氏、德妃徒單氏、柔妃大氏俱陪葬於坤厚陵。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the twenty-eighth year, she was jointly buried at Kunhou Mausoleum together with Virtuous Consort Shimoshi, Virtuous Consort Tudan, and Gentle Consort Dashi.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the twenty-eighth year she was jointly buried at Kunhou Mausoleum together with Virtuous Consort Shimoshi, Virtuous Consort Tudan, and Gentle Consort Dashi.

sentences.zh: 衛紹王即位，追諡光獻皇后，贈妃弟獻可特進。

translations.literal: When Emperor Weishao took the throne, she was posthumously titled Empress Guangxian; the consort's younger brother Xiank was granted Special Advancement.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Weishao took the throne, she was posthumously titled Empress Guangxian; the consort's younger brother Xiank was granted Special Advancement.

sentences.zh: 貞祐三年九月，削皇后號。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the third year of Zhenyou, her empress title was stripped.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the third year of Zhenyou her empress title was stripped.

sentences.zh: 顯宗孝懿皇后

translations.literal: Empress Xiaoyi of Emperor Xianzong
translations.idiomatic: Empress Xiaoyi of Emperor Xianzong

sentences.zh: 徒單氏。

translations.literal: She was of the Tudan clan.
translations.idiomatic: She was of the Tudan clan.

sentences.zh: 其先忒裏辟刺人也。

translations.literal: Her forebears were people of Telipici.
translations.idiomatic: Her forebears were people of Telipici.

sentences.zh: 曾祖抄，從太祖取遼有功，命以所部為猛安，世襲之。

translations.literal: Her great-grandfather Chao, who followed Emperor Taizu in taking Liao with merit, was ordered to make his command a meng'an, hereditarily transmitted.
translations.idiomatic: Her great-grandfather Chao followed Emperor Taizu in the conquest of Liao with merit and was ordered to make his command a hereditary meng'an.

sentences.zh: 祖婆盧火，以戰功多，累官開府儀同三司，贈司徒、齊國公。

translations.literal: Her grandfather Poluhuo, for many military achievements, rose through offices to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness Bearing the Golden Pocket with Purse Set, and was posthumously granted Minister of Education and Duke of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Her grandfather Poluhuo, for many military achievements, rose to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness Bearing the Golden Pocket with Purse Set and was posthumously granted Minister of Education and Duke of Qi.

sentences.zh: 父貞，尚遼王宗幹女梁國公主，加駙馬都尉，贈太師、廣平郡王。

translations.literal: Her father Zhen married the Princess of Liang State, daughter of Liao Prince Zonggan, was made Commandant Escorting the Imperial Son-in-Law, and was posthumously granted Grand Preceptor and Prince of Guangping Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Her father Zhen married the Princess of Liang State, daughter of Liao Prince Zonggan, was made Commandant Escorting the Imperial Son-in-Law, and was posthumously granted Grand Preceptor and Prince of Guangping Commandery.

sentences.zh: 后以皇統七年生於遼陽。

translations.literal: The empress was born in Liaoyang in the seventh year of Huangtong.
translations.idiomatic: The empress was born in Liaoyang in the seventh year of Huangtong.

sentences.zh: 母夢神人授以寶珠，光焰滿室，既寤而生，紅光燭於庭。

translations.literal: Her mother dreamed a divine being gave her a precious pearl; radiance filled the room; when she awoke she gave birth, and red light illuminated the courtyard.
translations.idiomatic: Her mother dreamed that a divine being gave her a precious pearl and radiance filled the room; when she awoke she gave birth, and red light illuminated the courtyard.

sentences.zh: 后性莊重寡言，父母嘗令總家事，細大畢辦，諸男不及也。

translations.literal: The empress was by nature dignified and sparing of words; her parents once put her in charge of the whole household; great and small matters she completed entirely, beyond what the sons could do.
translations.idiomatic: She was dignified and sparing of words; her parents once put her in charge of the household, and great and small matters she handled completely—better than any of her brothers.

sentences.zh: 世宗初即位，貞為御史大夫，自南京馳見。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shizong first took the throne, Zhen was Censor-in-Chief and galloped from the Southern Capital to see him.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shizong first took the throne, Zhen was Censor-in-Chief and galloped from the Southern Capital to see him.

sentences.zh: 世宗喜謂之曰：「卿雖廢主腹心臣，然未嘗助彼為虐，況卿家法可尚，其以卿女為朕子妃。」

translations.literal: Emperor Shizong said to him with pleasure: "Though you were a trusted minister of the deposed ruler, you never aided him in cruelty; moreover your family's standards are worthy of esteem—take your daughter as consort to my son."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizong said to him with pleasure, "Though you were a trusted minister of the deposed ruler, you never aided him in cruelty; moreover your family's standards are worthy of esteem—let your daughter become my son's consort."

sentences.zh: 及顯宗為皇太子，大定四年九月，備禮親迎于貞弟。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xianzong became Crown Prince, in the ninth month of the fourth year of Dading the full rites of personal welcome were performed at Zhen's younger brother's residence.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xianzong became Crown Prince, in the ninth month of the fourth year of Dading the full rites of personal welcome were performed at Zhen's younger brother's residence.

sentences.zh: 世宗臨宴，盡歡而罷。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizong attended the feast and dismissed it only when all had rejoiced to the full.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizong attended the feast and dismissed it only when all had rejoiced to the full.

sentences.zh: 是年十一月，顯宗生辰，初封為皇太子妃。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of that year, on Emperor Xianzong's birthday, she was first enfeoffed as Crown Princess Consort.
translations.idiomatic: That November, on Emperor Xianzong's birthday, she was first enfeoffed as Crown Princess Consort.

sentences.zh: 八年七月，上遣宣徽使移刺神獨斡以名馬、寶刀、禦饍賜太子及妃，仍諭之曰：「妃今臨蓐，願平安得雄。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the eighth year, the Emperor sent Palace Commissioner Yila Shenduwo with famous horses, precious swords, and imperial viands to bestow on the Crown Prince and consort, and further instructed them: "The consort is now near childbirth; may she be safe and bear a male.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the eighth year the Emperor sent Palace Commissioner Yila Shenduwo with famous horses, precious swords, and imperial viands for the Crown Prince and consort, and instructed them, "The consort is near childbirth; may she be safe and bear a son.

sentences.zh: 有慶之後，宜以此刀置左右。」

translations.literal: After the happy event, this sword should be kept at hand."
translations.idiomatic: After the happy event, keep this sword at hand."

sentences.zh: 既而皇孫生，是為章宗。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward the imperial grandson was born—this was Emperor Zhangzong.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward the imperial grandson was born—this was Emperor Zhangzong.

sentences.zh: 時上幸金蓮川，次冰井，翌日，上臨幸撫視，宴甚歡。

translations.literal: At the time the Emperor was at Jinlianchuan and halted at Bingjing; the next day he visited in person to comfort them and feasted with great joy.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the Emperor was at Jinlianchuan and halted at Bingjing; the next day he visited in person to comfort them and feasted with great joy.

sentences.zh: 又賜禦服佩刀等物，謂顯宗曰：「祖宗積慶，且皇后陰德至厚，而有今日，社稷之洪福也。」

translations.literal: He further bestowed imperial garments, belt swords, and the like, and said to Emperor Xianzong: "Our ancestors' accumulated blessing, and moreover the empress's hidden virtue is exceedingly deep—hence today; this is the great fortune of altars and state."
translations.idiomatic: He further bestowed imperial garments, belt swords, and the like, and told Emperor Xianzong, "Our ancestors' accumulated blessing, and the empress's hidden virtue so deep—hence this day; it is the great fortune of altars and state."

sentences.zh: 又謂李石、紇石烈志寧曰：「朕諸子雖多，皇后止有太子一人而已。

translations.literal: He also said to Li Shi and Hesilie Zhining: "Though I have many sons, the empress has only the Crown Prince alone.
translations.idiomatic: He also told Li Shi and Hesilie Zhining, "Though I have many sons, the empress has borne only the Crown Prince.

sentences.zh: 今幸得嫡孫，觀其骨相不凡，又生麻達葛山，山勢衍氣清，朕甚嘉之。」

translations.literal: Now we are fortunate to obtain a legitimate grandson; observing his bone structure it is extraordinary; moreover he was born at Mount Madage; the mountain's contours extend and its qi is clear—I greatly commend this."
translations.idiomatic: Now we are fortunate to have a legitimate grandson; his bone structure is extraordinary, and he was born at Mount Madage, whose contours extend and whose qi is clear—I greatly commend this."

sentences.zh: 因以山名為章宗小字。

translations.literal: Thereupon he took the mountain's name as Zhangzong's childhood name.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he took the mountain's name as Zhangzong's childhood name.

sentences.zh: 后素謙謹，每畏其家世崇寵，見父母流涕而言曰：「高明之家，古人所忌，願善自保持。」

translations.literal: The empress was always modest and cautious, ever fearing her family's exalted favor; seeing her parents she wept and said: "Households of lofty eminence are what the ancients dreaded—may you well preserve yourselves."
translations.idiomatic: The empress was always modest and cautious, ever fearing her family's exalted favor; seeing her parents she wept and said, "Households of lofty eminence are what the ancients dreaded—may you preserve yourselves well."

sentences.zh: 其後，家果以海陵事敗，盡其遠慮如此。

translations.literal: Later, the family indeed fell through the affair of Emperor Hailing—her far-sightedness was complete in this.
translations.idiomatic: Later the family indeed fell through the affair of Emperor Hailing—her far-sightedness was complete.

sentences.zh: 世宗嘗謂諸王妃、公主曰：「皇太子妃容止合度，服飾得中，爾等當法效之。」

translations.literal: Emperor Shizong once told the various princes' consorts and princesses: "The Crown Princess Consort's bearing and deportment are fitting, her dress and adornment are moderate—you should take her as model."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizong once told the various princes' consorts and princesses, "The Crown Princess Consort's bearing is fitting and her dress moderate—you should take her as your model."

sentences.zh: 章宗即位，尊為皇太后，更所居仁壽宮名曰隆慶宮。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhangzong took the throne, she was honored as Empress Dowager; the palace where she resided, Renshou Palace, was renamed Longqing Palace.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhangzong took the throne she was honored as Empress Dowager; her residence Renshou Palace was renamed Longqing Palace.

sentences.zh: 詔有司歲奉金千兩、銀五千兩、重幣五百端、絹二千疋、綿二萬兩、布五百疋、錢五萬貫。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the officials yearly to present one thousand taels of gold, five thousand taels of silver, five hundred bolts of heavy silks, two thousand bolts of plain silk, twenty thousand taels of cotton, five hundred bolts of cloth, and fifty thousand strings of cash.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered officials yearly to present one thousand taels of gold, five thousand taels of silver, five hundred bolts of heavy silks, two thousand bolts of plain silk, twenty thousand taels of cotton, five hundred bolts of cloth, and fifty thousand strings of cash.

sentences.zh: 他所應用，內庫奉之，毋拘其數。

translations.literal: Whatever else was needed, the inner treasury supplied it without limiting the amount.
translations.idiomatic: Whatever else she needed, the inner treasury supplied without limit.

sentences.zh: 上月或五朝六朝，而后愈加敬儉，見諸大長公主，禮如平時，惇睦九族，恩紀皆合。

translations.literal: The Emperor visited her five or six times a month, yet the empress became all the more respectful and frugal; meeting the various senior grand princesses, her courtesy was as in ordinary times; she was warm to the nine clans and her bonds of kindness were all in accord.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor visited her five or six times a month, yet she became all the more respectful and frugal; meeting the senior grand princesses she showed the same courtesy as always; she was warm to the nine clans and her bonds of kindness were all in accord.

sentences.zh: 尤惡聞人過，諛佞之言無所得入。

translations.literal: She especially hated hearing of others' faults; flattering and fawning words found no entry.
translations.idiomatic: She especially hated hearing of others' faults; flattering words found no entry.

sentences.zh: 恕以容物，未嘗見喜慍。

translations.literal: She forgave and accommodated others and was never seen pleased or angry.
translations.idiomatic: She forgave and accommodated others and was never seen pleased or angry.

sentences.zh: 然禦下公平，雖至親無所阿徇。

translations.literal: Yet in governing subordinates she was fair; even toward the closest kin she showed no partiality.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in governing subordinates she was fair; even toward the closest kin she showed no partiality.

sentences.zh: 嘗誡諸侄曰：「皇帝以我故，乃推恩外家，當盡忠圖報。

translations.literal: She once admonished her nephews: "The Emperor, because of me, extends favor to our maternal kin—you should exhaust loyalty and plan repayment.
translations.idiomatic: She once admonished her nephews, "The Emperor extends favor to our kin because of me—you must serve with full loyalty.

sentences.zh: 勿謂小善為無益而弗為，小惡為無傷而弗去。

translations.literal: Do not think a small good is without benefit and fail to do it; do not think a small evil is without harm and fail to remove it.
translations.idiomatic: Do not think a small good is without benefit and fail to do it; do not think a small evil is without harm and fail to remove it.

sentences.zh: 毋藉吾之貴，輒肆非違，以幹國家常憲。」

translations.literal: Do not rely on my exalted status and then recklessly commit wrongdoing, thereby violating the dynasty's standing statutes."
translations.idiomatic: Do not rely on my exalted status and recklessly commit wrongdoing, thereby violating the dynasty's standing statutes."

sentences.zh: 一日，妹並國夫人、嫂涇國夫人等侍側，因諭之曰：「爾家累素重，且非豐厚，宜節約財用，勿以吾為可恃。

translations.literal: One day, her younger sister the Lady of Bing State, her sister-in-law the Lady of Jing State, and others attended at her side; she instructed them: "Your family burdens have always been heavy and are not ample—you should economize wealth and must not think me someone to be relied upon.
translations.idiomatic: One day her younger sister the Lady of Bing State, her sister-in-law the Lady of Jing State, and others attended at her side; she told them, "Your family burdens have always been heavy and your means are not ample—economize your wealth and do not think me someone to be relied upon.

sentences.zh: 吾受天下之養，豈有所私積哉。

translations.literal: I receive the empire's sustenance—how could I have private accumulations?
translations.idiomatic: I receive the empire's sustenance—how could I have private accumulations?

sentences.zh: 況財用者，天下之財用也。

translations.literal: Moreover wealth is the empire's wealth.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover wealth is the empire's wealth.

sentences.zh: 吾終不能多取以富爾之私室。」

translations.literal: I ultimately cannot take more to enrich your private households."
translations.idiomatic: I cannot take more to enrich your private households."

sentences.zh: 家人有以玉盂進者，卻之，且曰：「貴異物而殫財用，非我所欲也。

translations.literal: When a family member presented a jade bowl, she refused it and said: "Valuing rare objects and exhausting wealth is not what I desire.
translations.idiomatic: When a family member presented a jade bowl, she refused it and said, "Valuing rare objects and exhausting wealth is not what I desire.

sentences.zh: 況我之賜予有度，今爾以此為獻，何以自給。

translations.literal: Moreover my gifts have measure; now you offer this—how will you support yourselves?
translations.idiomatic: Moreover my gifts are measured; now you offer this—how will you support yourselves?

sentences.zh: 徒費汝財，我實無用，後勿複爾。」

translations.literal: You waste only your wealth; I truly have no use for it—hereafter do not do this again."
translations.idiomatic: You waste only your wealth; I have no use for it—do not do this again."

sentences.zh: 明昌元年，禮官議以五月奉上冊寶，后弗許。

translations.literal: In the first year of Mingchang, ritual officials proposed presenting the seal and regalia in the fifth month; the empress did not consent.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Mingchang ritual officials proposed presenting the seal and regalia in the fifth month; the empress did not consent.

sentences.zh: 上屢為之請，后曰：「今世宗服未終，遽衣錦繡、佩珠玉，于禮何安。

translations.literal: The Emperor repeatedly requested it on her behalf; the empress said: "Now Emperor Shizong's mourning is not yet ended—suddenly to wear brocade and silk and adorn with pearls and jade—how could ritual be at ease?
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor repeatedly requested it; she said, "Emperor Shizong's mourning is not yet ended—how could ritual permit me suddenly to wear brocade and adorn myself with pearls and jade?

sentences.zh: 當俟服闋行之。」

translations.literal: We should wait until mourning is concluded before proceeding."
translations.idiomatic: We should wait until mourning is concluded."

sentences.zh: 上諭有司曰：「太后執意甚堅，其待來年。」

translations.literal: The Emperor instructed the officials: "The Empress Dowager's resolve is very firm—let it wait until next year."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor instructed officials, "The Empress Dowager's resolve is very firm—let it wait until next year."

sentences.zh: 明昌二年正月，崩于隆慶宮，年四十五。

translations.literal: In the first month of the second year of Mingchang, she died at Longqing Palace, aged forty-five.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the second year of Mingchang she died at Longqing Palace, aged forty-five.

sentences.zh: 諡曰孝懿，祔葬裕陵。

translations.literal: Her posthumous title was Xiaoyi; she was jointly buried at Yuling.
translations.idiomatic: Her posthumous title was Xiaoyi; she was jointly buried at Yuling.

sentences.zh: 后好《詩》、《書》，尤喜《老》、《莊》，學純淡清懿，造次心於禮。

translations.literal: The empress loved the Odes and Documents and especially delighted in the Laozi and Zhuangzi; her learning was pure, mild, and clear in virtue; even in haste her mind was on ritual.
translations.idiomatic: She loved the Odes and Documents and especially delighted in the Laozi and Zhuangzi; her learning was pure and serene; even in haste her mind was on ritual.

sentences.zh: 逮嬪禦以和平，其有生子而母亡者，視之如己所生，慈訓無間。

translations.literal: Toward palace women she was peaceful; when any bore a child whose mother died, she regarded it as her own offspring, her nurturing instruction without gap.
translations.idiomatic: Toward palace women she was peaceful; when any bore a child whose mother had died, she regarded it as her own, her nurturing without stint.

sentences.zh: 上時問安，見事有未當者，必加之嚴誡雲。

translations.literal: When the Emperor came to inquire after her health, if he saw anything not fitting, she would surely add stern admonition.
translations.idiomatic: When the Emperor came to inquire after her health, if he saw anything amiss she would add stern admonition.

sentences.zh: 顯宗昭聖皇后

translations.literal: Empress Zhaosheng of Emperor Xianzong
translations.idiomatic: Empress Zhaosheng of Emperor Xianzong

sentences.zh: 昭聖皇后，劉氏，遼陽人。

translations.literal: Empress Zhaosheng, surname Liu, a native of Liaoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Zhaosheng, née Liu, was a native of Liaoyang.

sentences.zh: 天眷二年九月己亥夜，后家若見有黃衣女子入其母室中者，俄頃，后生。

translations.literal: On the night of jihai day in the ninth month of the second year of Tianjuan, the empress's household seemed to see a woman in yellow enter her mother's chamber; shortly afterward the empress was born.
translations.idiomatic: On the night of jihai day in the ninth month of the second year of Tianjuan, her household seemed to see a woman in yellow enter her mother's chamber; shortly afterward she was born.

sentences.zh: 性聰慧，凡字過目不忘。

translations.literal: By nature intelligent, any character once seen she did not forget.
translations.idiomatic: She was intelligent; any character she saw once she never forgot.

sentences.zh: 初讀《孝經》，旬日終卷。

translations.literal: When she first read the Classic of Filial Piety, in ten days she finished the scroll.
translations.idiomatic: When she first read the Classic of Filial Piety, she finished the scroll in ten days.

sentences.zh: 最喜佛書。

translations.literal: She most delighted in Buddhist texts.
translations.idiomatic: She most delighted in Buddhist texts.

sentences.zh: 世宗為東京留守，因擊球，見而奇之，使見貞懿皇后于府中，進退閒雅，無恣睢之色。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shizong was Military Governor of the Eastern Capital, while playing polo he saw her and found her extraordinary; he had her presented to Empress Zhenyi at the residence; in advancing and retreating she was easy and elegant, without a look of arrogance.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shizong was Military Governor of the Eastern Capital, he saw her while playing polo and found her extraordinary; he had her presented to Empress Zhenyi at the residence; in advancing and retreating she was easy and elegant, without a trace of arrogance.

sentences.zh: 大定元年，選入東宮，時年二十三。

translations.literal: In the first year of Dading she was selected into the Eastern Palace; she was then twenty-three.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Dading she was selected into the Eastern Palace at the age of twenty-three.

sentences.zh: 三年三月十三日，宣宗生。

translations.literal: On the thirteenth day of the third month of the third year, Emperor Xuanzong was born.
translations.idiomatic: On the thirteenth day of the third month of the third year Emperor Xuanzong was born.

sentences.zh: 是日，大雨震電，后驚悸得疾，尋卒。

translations.literal: That day, great rain and thunder and lightning; the empress, startled and shaken, fell ill and soon died.
translations.idiomatic: That day brought great rain, thunder, and lightning; the empress, startled and shaken, fell ill and soon died.

sentences.zh: 承安五年，贈裕陵昭華。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Cheng'an, [she was] ennobled as Zhaohua of Yuling.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Cheng'an she was posthumously ennobled as Zhaohua of Yuling.

sentences.zh: 宣宗即位，追尊為皇太后，升祔顯宗廟，追諡昭聖皇后。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuanzong ascended the throne, [she was] posthumously honored as Empress Dowager, her spirit tablet was elevated and placed in Xianzong's temple, and she was posthumously titled Empress Zhaosheng.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuanzong ascended the throne, she was posthumously honored as Empress Dowager, her spirit tablet was installed in Xianzong's temple, and she received the posthumous title Empress Zhaosheng.

sentences.zh: 章宗欽懷皇后

translations.literal: Empress Qinhuai of Emperor Zhangzong
translations.idiomatic: Empress Qinhuai of Emperor Zhangzong

sentences.zh: 章宗欽懷皇后，蒲察氏，上京路曷速河人也。

translations.literal: Empress Qinhuai of Emperor Zhangzong, of the Pucha clan, was a native of Yasuhe in Shangjing Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Qinhuai of Emperor Zhangzong, née Pucha, was a native of Yasuhe in Shangjing Circuit.

sentences.zh: 曾署祖太神，國初有功，累階光祿大夫，贈司空、應國公。

translations.literal: Her great-grandfather was named Taishen; he had merit at the founding of the state, rose through the ranks to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, and was posthumously given the titles of Minister of Works and Duke of Ying.
translations.idiomatic: Her great-grandfather Taishen had merit at the founding of the dynasty, rose through the ranks to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, and was posthumously given the titles of Minister of Works and Duke of Ying.

sentences.zh: 祖阿胡迭，官至特進，贈司徒、譙國公。

translations.literal: Her grandfather Ahudie reached the rank of Special Advancement and was posthumously given the titles of Minister over the Masses and Duke of Qiao.
translations.idiomatic: Her grandfather Ahudie reached the rank of Special Advancement and was posthumously given the titles of Minister over the Masses and Duke of Qiao.

sentences.zh: 父鼎壽尚熙宗鄭國公主，授駙馬都尉、中都路昏得渾山猛安、曷速木單世襲謀克，累官至金吾衛上將軍，贈太尉、越國公。

translations.literal: Her father Dingshou married Princess Zheng of Emperor Xizong; he was appointed Commandant of the Feathered Forest Imperial Son-in-law, made Military Colony Commandant of Hundeshan in the Central Capital Circuit and hereditary Commander of Yasu Wood Single, rose through the ranks to Grand General of the Golden Wu Guard, and was posthumously given the titles of Grand Commandant and Duke of Yue.
translations.idiomatic: Her father Dingshou married Princess Zheng of Emperor Xizong; he was appointed Commandant of the Feathered Forest Imperial Son-in-law, made Military Colony Commandant of Hundeshan in the Central Capital Circuit and hereditary Commander of Yasu Wood Single, rose through the ranks to Grand General of the Golden Wu Guard, and was posthumously given the titles of Grand Commandant and Duke of Yue.

sentences.zh: 后之始生，有紅光被體，移時不退。

translations.literal: At the empress's birth, red light covered her body and for a long while did not fade.
translations.idiomatic: At her birth red light covered her body and for a long while did not fade.

sentences.zh: 就養于姨冀國公主，既長，孝謹如事所生。

translations.literal: She was raised by her aunt, Princess Ji of Ji State; once grown, in filial piety and care she was as toward her own mother.
translations.idiomatic: She was raised by her aunt, Princess Ji of Ji State; once grown, she was as filial and careful toward her as toward her own mother.

sentences.zh: 大定二十三年，章宗為金源郡王，行納采禮。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year of Dading, when Zhangzong was Prince of Jinyuan Commandery, the betrothal ceremony was performed.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year of Dading, when Zhangzong was Prince of Jinyuan Commandery, the betrothal ceremony was performed.

sentences.zh: 世宗遣近侍局使徒單懷忠就賜金百兩、銀千兩、廄馬六匹、重彩三十端。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizong sent Tudan Huaizhong, Commissioner of the Inner Attendance Bureau, to bestow there one hundred taels of gold, one thousand taels of silver, six stable horses, and thirty bolts of heavy silk.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizong sent Tudan Huaizhong, Commissioner of the Inner Attendance Bureau, to bestow one hundred taels of gold, one thousand taels of silver, six stable horses, and thirty bolts of heavy silk.

sentences.zh: 拜命間，慶雲見於日側，觀者異之。

translations.literal: While she received the command, auspicious clouds appeared beside the sun; onlookers marveled at it.
translations.idiomatic: While she received the command, auspicious clouds appeared beside the sun, and onlookers marveled.

sentences.zh: 是年十一月，備禮親迎。

translations.literal: That year in the eleventh month, full rites were prepared and she was received in person at the wedding.
translations.idiomatic: That year, in the eleventh month, full rites were prepared and she was received in person at the wedding.

sentences.zh: 詔親王宰執三品已上官及命婦會禮，封金源郡王夫人，后進封妃，崩。

translations.literal: An edict summoned princes, chief ministers, officials of third rank and above, and titled ladies to attend the ceremony; she was enfeoffed as Lady of Prince of Jinyuan Commandery, later advanced to consort rank, and died.
translations.idiomatic: An edict summoned princes, chief ministers, officials of third rank and above, and titled ladies to attend the ceremony; she was enfeoffed as Lady of the Prince of Jinyuan Commandery, later advanced to consort rank, and died.

sentences.zh: 后性淑明，風儀粹穆，知讀書為文。

translations.literal: The empress's nature was gentle and bright, her bearing pure and solemn; she knew how to read and compose texts.
translations.idiomatic: She was gentle and bright by nature, pure and solemn in bearing, and knew how to read and compose texts.

sentences.zh: 帝即位，遂加追冊，仍詔告中外，奉安神主于坤甯宮，歲時致祭。

translations.literal: When the Emperor ascended the throne, he at once added posthumous enrollment; he also issued an edict proclaiming it within and without, installed her spirit tablet in Kunning Palace, and offered sacrifices at the seasons.
translations.idiomatic: When the Emperor ascended the throne, he at once added posthumous enrollment, issued an edict proclaiming it throughout the realm, installed her spirit tablet in Kunning Palace, and offered seasonal sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 大安初，祔於道陵。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Da'an, she was jointly buried at Daoling.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Da'an she was jointly buried at Daoling.

sentences.zh: 章宗元妃李氏

translations.literal: First Consort Li of Emperor Zhangzong
translations.idiomatic: First Consort Li of Emperor Zhangzong

sentences.zh: 元妃李氏師兒，其家有罪，沒入宮籍監。

translations.literal: First Consort Li, called Shier—their family had committed a crime and was enrolled in the palace household register as supervised persons.
translations.idiomatic: First Consort Li, called Shier, came from a family that had committed a crime and was enrolled in the palace household register as supervised persons.

sentences.zh: 父湘，母王盻兒，皆微賤。

translations.literal: Her father was Xiang and her mother Wang Pan'er; both were of humble and low status.
translations.idiomatic: Her father was Xiang and her mother Wang Pan'er; both were of humble and low status.

sentences.zh: 大定末，以監戶女子入宮。

translations.literal: At the end of Dading, as the daughter of a supervised household she entered the palace.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Dading she entered the palace as the daughter of a supervised household.

sentences.zh: 是時宮教張建教宮中，師兒與諸宮女皆從之學。

translations.literal: At that time the palace instructor Zhang Jian taught within the palace; Shier and all the palace women studied under him.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the palace instructor Zhang Jian taught within the palace; Shier and all the palace women studied under him.

sentences.zh: 故事，宮教以青紗隔障蔽內外，宮教居障外，諸宮女居障內，不得面見。

translations.literal: By precedent, the palace instructor used a green gauze screen to divide inner and outer; the instructor sat outside the screen and the palace women inside, and they could not meet face to face.
