translations.idiomatic: By precedent the palace instructor used a green gauze screen to divide inner from outer; the instructor sat outside the screen and the palace women inside, and they could not meet face to face.

sentences.zh: 有不識字及問義，皆自障內映紗指字請問，宮教自障外口說教之。

translations.literal: When any did not know a character or asked about meaning, all from within the screen would point at characters through the gauze to inquire; the instructor from outside the screen would teach them orally.
translations.idiomatic: When any did not know a character or asked about meaning, they would point at characters through the gauze from within the screen to inquire, and the instructor would teach them orally from outside.

sentences.zh: 諸女子中惟師兒易為領解，建不知其誰，但識其音聲清亮。

translations.literal: Among all the women only Shier was easily able to grasp meaning; Jian did not know which one she was, but recognized her voice as clear and bright.
translations.idiomatic: Among all the women only Shier grasped the lessons easily; Jian did not know which one she was, but recognized her voice as clear and bright.

sentences.zh: 章宗嘗問建，宮教中女子誰可教者。

translations.literal: Zhangzong once asked Jian which of the women under palace instruction were teachable.
translations.idiomatic: Zhangzong once asked Jian which of the women under palace instruction were most teachable.

sentences.zh: 建對曰：「就中聲音清亮者最可教。」

translations.literal: Jian replied: "Among them, the one whose voice is clear and bright is most teachable."
translations.idiomatic: Jian replied, "Among them, the one whose voice is clear and bright is most teachable."

sentences.zh: 章宗以建言求得之。

translations.literal: Zhangzong, from this report, found and obtained her.
translations.idiomatic: From this report Zhangzong found and obtained her.

sentences.zh: 宦者梁道譽師兒才美，勸章宗納之。

translations.literal: The eunuch Liang Daoyu praised Shier's talent and beauty and urged Zhangzong to take her in.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuch Liang Daoyu praised Shier's talent and beauty and urged Zhangzong to take her in.

sentences.zh: 章宗好文辭，妃性慧黠，能作字，知文義，尤善伺候顏色，迎合旨意，遂大愛幸。

translations.literal: Zhangzong loved literary composition; the consort was clever and quick-witted, could write characters, understood literary meaning, and was especially skilled at reading his mood and matching his wishes—thus she came to be greatly favored.
translations.idiomatic: Zhangzong loved literary composition; the consort was clever and quick-witted, could write, understood literary meaning, and was especially skilled at reading his mood and matching his wishes, and so came to be greatly favored.

sentences.zh: 明昌四年，封為昭容。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Mingchang she was enfeoffed as Palace Acolyte.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Mingchang she was enfeoffed as Palace Acolyte.

sentences.zh: 明年，進封淑妃，父湘追贈金紫光祿大夫、上柱國、隴西郡公。

translations.literal: The next year she was advanced to Pure Consort; her father Xiang was posthumously given the titles of Grand Master of Golden Light and Purplish Radiance, Supreme Pillar of the State, and Duke of Longxi Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: The next year she was advanced to Pure Consort; her father Xiang was posthumously given the titles of Grand Master of Golden Light and Purplish Radiance, Supreme Pillar of the State, and Duke of Longxi Commandery.

sentences.zh: 祖父、曾祖父皆追贈。

translations.literal: Her grandfather and great-grandfather were both posthumously ennobled.
translations.idiomatic: Her grandfather and great-grandfather were both posthumously ennobled.

sentences.zh: 兄喜兒舊嘗為盜，與弟鐵哥皆擢顯近，勢傾朝廷，風采動四方，射利競進之徒爭趨走其門，南京李炳、中山李著與通譜系，超取顯美。

translations.literal: Her elder brother Xier had once been a bandit; he and her younger brother Tiege were both promoted to eminent positions close to power; their influence tilted the court, their prestige moved all four quarters; those who sought profit and advancement raced to their door; Li Bing of Nanjing and Li Zhu of Zhongshan, who claimed kinship through the same genealogy, were abruptly promoted to prominent and fine offices.
translations.idiomatic: Her elder brother Xier had once been a bandit; he and her younger brother Tiege were both promoted to eminent positions close to power; their influence tilted the court and their prestige moved all four quarters; those who sought profit and advancement raced to their door; Li Bing of Nanjing and Li Zhu of Zhongshan, who claimed kinship through the same genealogy, were abruptly promoted to prominent offices.

sentences.zh: 胥持國附依以致宰相。

translations.literal: Xu Chiguo, attaching himself to them, rose to become Chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Chiguo, attaching himself to them, rose to become Chancellor.

sentences.zh: 怙財固位，上下紛然，知其奸蠹，不敢擊之，雖擊之，莫能去也。

translations.literal: Relying on wealth to hold their posts, they threw court and populace into disorder; though people knew their wicked corruption, none dared strike at them—and even when struck at, they could not be removed.
translations.idiomatic: Relying on wealth to hold their posts, they threw court and populace into disorder; though people knew their wicked corruption, none dared strike at them, and even when struck at they could not be removed.

sentences.zh: 紇石烈執中貪愎不法，章宗知其跋扈，而屢斥屢起，終亂天下。

translations.literal: Heshilie Zhizhong was greedy, obstinate, and lawless; Zhangzong knew his overbearing nature, yet though repeatedly dismissed he was repeatedly restored, and in the end he threw the realm into chaos.
translations.idiomatic: Heshilie Zhizhong was greedy, obstinate, and lawless; Zhangzong knew his overbearing nature, yet though repeatedly dismissed he was repeatedly restored, and in the end he threw the realm into chaos.

sentences.zh: 自欽懷皇后沒世，中宮虛位久，章宗意屬李氏。

translations.literal: Since Empress Qinhuai's death the central palace had long stood vacant, and Zhangzong's mind was set on Lady Li.
translations.idiomatic: Since Empress Qinhuai's death the central palace had long stood vacant, and Zhangzong's mind was set on Lady Li.

sentences.zh: 而國朝故事，皆徒單、唐括、蒲察、拏懶僕散、紇石烈、烏林荅、烏古論諸部部長之家，世為姻婚，娶后尚主，而李氏微甚。

translations.literal: But by dynastic precedent empresses came from the chieftain families of the Tudan, Tangguo, Pucha, Nalan Pusan, Heshilie, Wulin, and Wugulun clans—generation after generation bound by marriage, supplying empresses and receiving imperial princesses in marriage—whereas the Li family was exceedingly humble.
translations.idiomatic: But by dynastic precedent empresses came from the chieftain families of the Tudan, Tangguo, Pucha, Nalan Pusan, Heshilie, Wulin, and Wugulun clans, generation after generation bound by marriage, supplying empresses and receiving imperial princesses in marriage, whereas the Li family was exceedingly humble.

sentences.zh: 至是，章宗果欲立之，大臣固執不從，台諫以為言，帝不得已，進封為元妃，而勢位熏赫，與皇后侔矣。

translations.literal: At this Zhangzong indeed wished to install her as empress; the chief ministers firmly refused; the censorate remonstrated; the Emperor, having no choice, advanced her to First Consort—but her power and position blazed forth until they matched the empress's.
translations.idiomatic: At this Zhangzong indeed wished to install her as empress; the chief ministers firmly refused and the censorate remonstrated; the Emperor, having no choice, advanced her to First Consort, but her power and position blazed forth until they matched the empress's.

sentences.zh: 一日，章宗宴宮中，優人瑇瑁頭者戲於前。

translations.literal: One day Zhangzong feasted in the palace, and a performer in a tortoiseshell cap played before them.
translations.idiomatic: One day Zhangzong feasted in the palace, and a performer in a tortoiseshell cap played before them.

sentences.zh: 或問：「上國有何符瑞？」

translations.literal: Someone asked: "What auspicious omens does the Upper State have?"
translations.idiomatic: Someone asked, "What auspicious omens does the Upper State have?"

sentences.zh: 優曰：「汝不聞鳳皇見乎。」

translations.literal: The performer said: "Have you not heard that the phoenix has appeared?"
translations.idiomatic: The performer said, "Have you not heard that the phoenix has appeared?"

sentences.zh: 其人曰：「知之，而未聞其詳。」

translations.literal: The man said: "I know of it, but have not heard the details."
translations.idiomatic: The man said, "I know of it, but have not heard the details."

sentences.zh: 優曰：「其飛有四，所應亦異。

translations.literal: The performer said: "Its flight has four modes, and the portents they answer to are also different.
translations.idiomatic: The performer said, "Its flight has four modes, and the portents they answer to are also different.

sentences.zh: 若響上飛則風雨順時，響下飛則五穀豐登，響外飛則四國來朝，向裏飛則加官進祿。」

translations.literal: If it flies echo-upward then wind and rain are timely; if echo-downward then the five grains are abundant; if echo-outward then the four states come to court; if inward-flying then rank and stipends are advanced."
translations.idiomatic: When it flies upward—through a pun on echo and direction—wind and rain come in season; downward, the five grains abound; outward, the four quarters send tribute; inward, offices rise and emoluments increase."

sentences.zh: 上笑而罷。

translations.literal: The Emperor laughed and let the matter drop.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor laughed and let the matter drop.

sentences.zh: 欽懷后及妃姬嘗有子，或二三歲或數月輒夭。

translations.literal: Empress Qinhuai and the consorts had borne children, but at two or three years or a few months they would perish.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Qinhuai and the consorts had borne children, but at two or three years, or a few months, they would perish.

sentences.zh: 承安五年，帝以繼嗣未立，禱禮太廟、山陵。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Cheng'an, because the heir had not been established, the Emperor performed prayer rites at the Grand Ancestral Temple and the imperial tombs.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Cheng'an, because the heir had not been established, the Emperor performed prayer rites at the Grand Ancestral Temple and the imperial tombs.

sentences.zh: 少府監張汝猷因轉對，奏「皇嗣未立，乞聖主親行禮事之後，遣近臣詣諸嶽觀廟祈禱。」

translations.literal: Director of the Palace Storehouse Zhang Youyou, on a rotation audience, memorialized: "The imperial heir is not yet established; I beg that after Your Majesty personally performs the rites, near ministers be sent to the sacred peaks, temples, and shrines to pray."
translations.idiomatic: Director of the Palace Storehouse Zhang Youyou, on a rotation audience, memorialized, "The imperial heir is not yet established; I beg that after Your Majesty personally performs the rites, near ministers be sent to the sacred peaks, temples, and shrines to pray."

sentences.zh: 詔司空襄往亳州禱太清宮，既而止之，遣刑部員外郎完顏匡往焉。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Minister of Works Xiang to go to Bozhou to pray at the Taiqing Palace; then this was stopped and Wanyan Kuang, Vice Director of the Ministry of Justice, was sent instead.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Minister of Works Xiang to go to Bozhou to pray at the Taiqing Palace; then this was stopped and Wanyan Kuang, Vice Director of the Ministry of Justice, was sent instead.

sentences.zh: 泰和二年八月丁酉，元妃生皇子忒鄰，群臣上表稱賀。

translations.literal: On dingyou day in the eighth month of the second year of Taihe, the First Consort bore the prince Tilie; the officials submitted congratulatory memorials.
translations.idiomatic: On dingyou day in the eighth month of the second year of Taihe, the First Consort bore the prince Tilie, and the officials submitted congratulatory memorials.

sentences.zh: 宴五品以上于神龍殿，六品以下宴於東廡下。

translations.literal: Those of fifth rank and above were feasted in the Divine Dragon Hall; those of sixth rank and below feasted beneath the eastern veranda.
translations.idiomatic: Those of fifth rank and above were feasted in the Divine Dragon Hall; those of sixth rank and below feasted beneath the eastern veranda.

sentences.zh: 詔平章政事徒單鎰報謝太廟，右丞完顏匡報謝山陵，使使亳州報謝太清宮。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Chief Councilor Tudan Yi to return thanks at the Grand Ancestral Temple, Vice Director Wanyan Kuang to return thanks at the imperial tombs, and emissaries to Bozhou to return thanks at the Taiqing Palace.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Chief Councilor Tudan Yi to return thanks at the Grand Ancestral Temple, Vice Director Wanyan Kuang to return thanks at the imperial tombs, and emissaries to Bozhou to return thanks at the Taiqing Palace.

sentences.zh: 既彌月，詔賜名，封為葛王。

translations.literal: Once the full month was complete, an edict bestowed a name and enfeoffed him as Prince of Ge.
translations.idiomatic: Once the full month was complete, an edict bestowed a name and enfeoffed him as Prince of Ge.

sentences.zh: 葛王，世宗初封，大定後不以封臣下，由是三等國號無葛。

translations.literal: Prince of Ge had been Shizong's initial enfeoffment; after Dading that title was not used to enfeoff subjects—thus among third-rank state names there was no Ge.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Ge had been Shizong's initial enfeoffment; after Dading that title was not used to enfeoff subjects, and so among third-rank state names there was no Ge.

sentences.zh: 尚書省奏，請于瀛王下附葛國號，上從之。

translations.literal: The Secretariat memorialized requesting that the state name Ge be attached under Prince of Ying; the Emperor assented.
translations.idiomatic: The Secretariat memorialized requesting that the state name Ge be attached under Prince of Ying, and the Emperor assented.

sentences.zh: 十二月癸酉，忒鄰生滿三月，敕放僧道度牒三千道，設醮于玄真觀，為忒鄰祈福。

translations.literal: On jiyou day in the twelfth month, when Tilie had completed three months since birth, an edict released three thousand ordination certificates for monks and Daoists, and a ritual was held at the Xuanyuan Abbey to pray for blessings for Tilie.
translations.idiomatic: On jiyou day in the twelfth month, when Tilie had completed three months since birth, an edict released three thousand ordination certificates for monks and Daoists, and a ritual was held at the Xuanyuan Abbey to pray for blessings for Tilie.

sentences.zh: 丁丑，禦慶和殿，浴皇子。

translations.literal: On dingchou day the Emperor attended at Qinghe Hall for the prince's bathing rite.
translations.idiomatic: On dingchou day the Emperor attended at Qinghe Hall for the prince's bathing rite.

sentences.zh: 詔百官用元旦禮儀進酒稱賀，五品以上進禮物。

translations.literal: An edict ordered all officials to offer wine and congratulations using New Year's ceremony; those of fifth rank and above presented gifts.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered all officials to offer wine and congratulations using New Year's ceremony; those of fifth rank and above presented gifts.

sentences.zh: 生凡二歲而薨。

translations.literal: He lived only two years before he died.
translations.idiomatic: He lived only two years before he died.

sentences.zh: 兄喜兒，累官宣徽使、安國軍節度使。

translations.literal: Her elder brother Xier rose through the offices to Commissioner of the Palace Endowment and Military Governor of Anguo Army.
translations.idiomatic: Her elder brother Xier rose through the offices to Commissioner of the Palace Endowment and Military Governor of Anguo Army.

sentences.zh: 弟鐵哥，累官近侍局使、少府監。

translations.literal: Her younger brother Tiege rose through the offices to Commissioner of the Inner Attendance Bureau and Director of the Palace Storehouse.
translations.idiomatic: Her younger brother Tiege rose through the offices to Commissioner of the Inner Attendance Bureau and Director of the Palace Storehouse.

sentences.zh: 至八年，承禦賈氏及範氏皆有娠，未及乳月，章宗已得嗽疾，頗困。

translations.literal: By the eighth year, Lady-in-Waiting Jia and Lady Fan were both pregnant; before they reached full term nursing, Zhangzong had contracted a coughing illness and was quite distressed.
translations.idiomatic: By the eighth year Lady-in-Waiting Jia and Lady Fan were both pregnant; before they reached full term, Zhangzong had contracted a coughing illness and was quite distressed.

sentences.zh: 是時衛王永濟自武定軍來朝。

translations.literal: At this time Prince Wei Yongji came to court from Wuding Army.
translations.idiomatic: At this time Prince Wei Yongji came to court from Wuding Army.

sentences.zh: 章宗於父兄中最愛衛王，欲使繼體立之，語在《衛紹王紀》。

translations.literal: Among his uncles and brothers Zhangzong loved Prince Wei most; he wished to have him succeed and install him—this is told in the Annals of Emperor Weishao.
translations.idiomatic: Among his uncles and brothers Zhangzong loved Prince Wei most and wished to have him succeed; this is told in the Annals of Emperor Weishao.

sentences.zh: 衛王朝辭，是日，章宗力疾與之擊球，謂衛王曰：「叔王不欲作主人，遽欲去邪？」

translations.literal: When Prince Wei came to court to take leave, that day Zhangzong, forcing himself despite illness, played polo with him and said to Prince Wei: "Uncle, you do not wish to play host—do you hurry to leave?"
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Wei came to court to take leave, that day Zhangzong, forcing himself despite illness, played polo with him and said to Prince Wei, "Uncle, you do not wish to play host—do you hurry to leave?"

sentences.zh: 元妃在傍，謂帝曰：「此非輕言者。」

translations.literal: The First Consort stood beside them and said to the Emperor: "These are not words to speak lightly."
translations.idiomatic: The First Consort stood beside them and said to the Emperor, "These are not words to speak lightly."

sentences.zh: 十一月乙卯，章宗大漸，衛王未發，元妃與黃門李新喜議立衛王，使內侍潘守恆召之。

translations.literal: On yimao day in the eleventh month Zhangzong was near death; Prince Wei had not yet departed; the First Consort and the Yellow Gate officer Li Xixin discussed installing Prince Wei and sent the inner attendant Pan Shoheng to summon him.
translations.idiomatic: On yimao day in the eleventh month Zhangzong was near death; Prince Wei had not yet departed; the First Consort and the Yellow Gate officer Li Xixin discussed installing Prince Wei and sent the inner attendant Pan Shoheng to summon him.

sentences.zh: 守恆頗知書，識大體，謂元妃曰：「此大事，當與大臣議。」

translations.literal: Shoheng was fairly learned and understood the larger matters; he said to the First Consort: "This is a great affair—it should be discussed with the chief ministers."
translations.idiomatic: Shoheng was fairly learned and understood the larger matters; he said to the First Consort, "This is a great affair—it should be discussed with the chief ministers."

sentences.zh: 乃使守恆召平章政事完顏匡。

translations.literal: He then had Shoheng summon Chief Councilor Wanyan Kuang.
translations.idiomatic: He then had Shoheng summon Chief Councilor Wanyan Kuang.

sentences.zh: 匡，顯宗侍讀，最為舊臣，有征伐功，故獨召之。

translations.literal: Kuang had been study companion to Xianzong, was the foremost senior minister, and had merit in military campaigns—therefore he alone was summoned.
translations.idiomatic: Kuang had been study companion to Xianzong, was the foremost senior minister, and had merit in military campaigns, and therefore he alone was summoned.

sentences.zh: 匡至，遂與定策立衛王。

translations.literal: When Kuang arrived, they at once settled the plan to install Prince Wei.
translations.idiomatic: When Kuang arrived, they at once settled the plan to install Prince Wei.

sentences.zh: 丙辰，章宗崩，遺詔皇叔衛王即皇帝位。

translations.literal: On bingchen day Zhangzong died; his final edict ordered his imperial uncle Prince Wei to ascend the throne.
translations.idiomatic: On bingchen day Zhangzong died; his final edict ordered his imperial uncle Prince Wei to ascend the throne.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「朕之內人，見有娠者兩位。

translations.literal: The edict said: "Among my inner consorts, two are presently pregnant.
translations.idiomatic: The edict said, "Among my inner consorts, two are presently pregnant.

sentences.zh: 如其中有男，當立為儲貳。

translations.literal: If among them there is a male, he should be established as heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: If among them there is a male, he should be established as heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 如皆是男子，擇可立者立之。」

translations.literal: If all are males, choose the one fit to install and install him."
translations.idiomatic: If all are males, choose the one fit to install and install him."

sentences.zh: 衛紹王即位，大安元年二月，詔曰：「章宗皇帝以天下重器畀於眇躬，遺旨謂掖庭內人有娠者兩位，如得男則立為儲貳。

translations.literal: When Emperor Weishao ascended the throne, in the second month of the first year of Da'an an edict said: "Emperor Zhangzong entrusted the weighty vessel of the realm to my humble person; his final instructions said that among the inner women of the rear palace two were pregnant—if a male was born he was to be established as heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Weishao ascended the throne, in the second month of the first year of Da'an an edict said, "Emperor Zhangzong entrusted the weighty vessel of the realm to my humble person; his final instructions said that among the inner women of the rear palace two were pregnant—if a male was born he was to be established as heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 申諭多方，皎如天日。

translations.literal: This was proclaimed in many places, bright as sun and moon.
translations.idiomatic: This was proclaimed in many places, bright as sun and moon.

sentences.zh: 朕雖涼菲，實受付託，思克副於遺意，每曲為之盡心，擇靜舍以俾居，遣懿親而守視。

translations.literal: Though I am slight and inadequate, I truly received this charge; thinking to fulfill his final wishes, I have bent every effort on their behalf—choosing quiet quarters for them to dwell in and sending honored kin to guard and watch over them.
translations.idiomatic: Though I am slight and inadequate, I truly received this charge; thinking to fulfill his final wishes, I have bent every effort on their behalf—choosing quiet quarters for them to dwell in and sending honored kin to guard and watch over them.

sentences.zh: 欽懷皇后母鄭國公主及乳母蕭國夫人晝夜不離。

translations.literal: Princess Zheng, mother of Empress Qinhuai, and the Wet Nurse, Lady Xiao of Xiao State, did not leave them day or night.
translations.idiomatic: Princess Zheng, mother of Empress Qinhuai, and the Wet Nurse, Lady Xiao of Xiao State, did not leave them day or night.

sentences.zh: 昨聞有爽于安養，已用軫憂而弗寧，爰命大臣專為調護。

translations.literal: Yesterday I heard that their safe nurturing had been disturbed; I have already been troubled and unquiet with concern, and therefore ordered chief ministers devoted solely to their care and adjustment.
translations.idiomatic: Yesterday I heard that their safe nurturing had been disturbed; I have already been troubled and unquiet with concern, and therefore ordered chief ministers devoted solely to their care.

sentences.zh: 今者平章政事僕散端、左丞孫即康奏言，承禦賈氏當以十一月免乳，今則已出三月，來事未可度知。

translations.literal: Now Chief Councilor Pusan Duan and Vice Director Sun Jikang memorialized that Lady-in-Waiting Jia should have completed nursing in the eleventh month; now three months have already passed—the coming outcome cannot yet be foreknown.
translations.idiomatic: Now Chief Councilor Pusan Duan and Vice Director Sun Jikang memorialized that Lady-in-Waiting Jia should have completed nursing in the eleventh month; now three months have already passed, and the coming outcome cannot yet be foreknown.

sentences.zh: 範氏產期，合在正月，而太醫副使儀師顏言，自年前十一月診得範氏胎氣有損，調治迄今，脈息雖和，胎形已失。

translations.literal: Lady Fan's term of delivery should fall in the first month; but Vice Commissioner of the Imperial Medical Service Yishi Yan said that since the eleventh month of the previous year he had diagnosed damage to Lady Fan's fetal qi; treated to the present, though the pulse was calm, the fetal form was already lost.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Fan's term of delivery should fall in the first month; but Vice Commissioner of the Imperial Medical Service Yishi Yan said that since the eleventh month of the previous year he had diagnosed damage to Lady Fan's fetal qi; treated to the present, though the pulse was calm, the fetal form was already lost.

sentences.zh: 及范氏自願於神御前削髮為尼。

translations.literal: Thereupon Lady Fan of her own will shaved her head and became a nun before the imperial spirit tablet.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Lady Fan of her own will shaved her head and became a nun before the imperial spirit tablet.

sentences.zh: 重念先皇帝重屬大事，豈期聞此，深用怛然。

translations.literal: Deeply recalling how the late Emperor greatly entrusted this great matter, who could expect to hear this—I am deeply dismayed.
translations.idiomatic: Deeply recalling how the late Emperor greatly entrusted this great matter, who could expect to hear this—I am deeply dismayed.

sentences.zh: 今範氏既已有損，而賈氏猶或可冀，告於先帝，願降靈禧，默賜保全，早生聖嗣。

translations.literal: Now that Lady Fan is already damaged, Lady Jia may still be hoped for; I report to the late Emperor, praying that his spirit descend in blessing, silently grant preservation, and that a sage heir be born soon.
translations.idiomatic: Now that Lady Fan is already damaged, Lady Jia may still be hoped for; I report to the late Emperor, praying that his spirit descend in blessing, silently grant preservation, and that a sage heir be born soon.

sentences.zh: 尚恐眾庶未究端由，要不匿於播敷，使咸明於吾意。」

translations.literal: Still fearing the multitude may not fully grasp the causes, I must not conceal this in proclamation—so that all may clearly understand my intent."
translations.idiomatic: Still fearing the multitude may not fully grasp the causes, I must not conceal this in proclamation, so that all may clearly understand my intent."

sentences.zh: 四月，詔曰：「近者有訴元妃李氏，潛計負恩，自泰和七年正月，章宗暫嘗違豫，李氏與新喜竊議，為儲嗣未立，欲令宮人詐作有身，計取他兒詐充皇嗣。

translations.literal: In the fourth month an edict said: "Recently there was a petition against First Consort Lady Li, who secretly plotted ingratitude: from the first month of the seventh year of Taihe, when Zhangzong was briefly unwell, Li and Xixin privately discussed that because the heir was not established, they wished to have palace women falsely claim pregnancy, planning to take another's child and falsely pass him off as the imperial heir.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month an edict said, "Recently there was a petition against First Consort Lady Li, who secretly plotted ingratitude: from the first month of the seventh year of Taihe, when Zhangzong was briefly unwell, Li and Xixin privately discussed that because the heir was not established, they wished to have palace women falsely claim pregnancy, planning to take another's child and falsely pass him off as the imperial heir.

sentences.zh: 遂於年前閏月十日，因賈承禦病嘔吐，腹中若有積塊，李氏與其母王盻兒及李新喜謀，令賈氏詐稱有身，俟將臨月，于李家取兒以入，月日不偶則規別取，以為皇嗣。

translations.literal: They then on the tenth day of the intercalary month before the year-end, exploiting Lady-in-Waiting Jia's illness and vomiting and a seeming mass in her belly, Li together with her mother Wang Pan'er and Li Xixin plotted to have Lady Jia falsely claim pregnancy; waiting until near term, they would take a child from the Li household and bring him in—if the month and day did not match they would plan to take another—to make him the imperial heir.
translations.idiomatic: They then on the tenth day of the intercalary month before the year-end, exploiting Lady-in-Waiting Jia's illness and vomiting and a seeming mass in her belly, Li together with her mother Wang Pan'er and Li Xixin plotted to have Lady Jia falsely claim pregnancy; waiting until near term, they would take a child from the Li household and bring him in—if the month and day did not match they would plan to take another—to make him the imperial heir.

sentences.zh: 章宗崩，謀不及行。

translations.literal: When Zhangzong died, the plot had no time to be carried out.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhangzong died, the plot had no time to be carried out.

sentences.zh: 當先帝彌留之際，命平章政事完顏匡都提點中外事務，明有敕旨，'我有兩宮人有娠'，更令召平章，左右並聞斯語。

translations.literal: At the moment the late Emperor was near death, he ordered Chief Councilor Wanyan Kuang to oversee all affairs within and without; there was a clear edict—'I have two palace women who are pregnant'—and he further ordered the Chief Councilor summoned; those at his side all heard these words.
translations.idiomatic: At the moment the late Emperor was near death, he ordered Chief Councilor Wanyan Kuang to oversee all affairs within and without; there was a clear edict—'I have two palace women who are pregnant'—and he further ordered the Chief Councilor summoned; those at his side all heard these words.

sentences.zh: 李氏並新喜乃敢不依敕旨，欲喚喜兒、鐵哥，事既不克，竊呼提點近侍局烏古論慶壽與計，因品藻諸王，議複不定。

translations.literal: Li and Xixin then dared not follow the edict; they wished to summon Xier and Tiege; when the affair could not succeed, they secretly called Wugulun Qingshou, overseer of the Inner Attendance Bureau, to consult; they appraised the various princes, and deliberation again could not be settled.
translations.idiomatic: Li and Xixin then dared not follow the edict; they wished to summon Xier and Tiege; when the affair could not succeed, they secretly called Wugulun Qingshou, overseer of the Inner Attendance Bureau, to consult; they appraised the various princes, and deliberation again could not be settled.

sentences.zh: 知近侍局副使徒單張僧遣人召平章，已到宣華門外，始發勘同。

translations.literal: Vice Commissioner of the Inner Attendance Bureau Tudan Zhangseng sent someone to summon the Chief Councilor; once he had reached outside Xuanhua Gate, deliberation was at last opened.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Commissioner of the Inner Attendance Bureau Tudan Zhangseng sent someone to summon the Chief Councilor; once he had reached outside Xuanhua Gate, deliberation was at last opened.

sentences.zh: 平章入內，一遵遺旨，以定大事。

translations.literal: The Chief Councilor entered within and, fully following the final instructions, settled the great affair.
translations.idiomatic: The Chief Councilor entered within and, fully following the final instructions, settled the great affair.

sentences.zh: 方先帝疾危，數召李氏，李氏不到。

translations.literal: Just when the late Emperor's illness was critical, he summoned Li many times; Li did not come.
translations.idiomatic: Just when the late Emperor's illness was critical, he summoned Li many times; Li did not come.

sentences.zh: 及索衣服，李氏承召亦不即來，猶與其母私議。

translations.literal: When clothes were requested, Li though summoned still did not come at once, but continued in private consultation with her mother.
translations.idiomatic: When clothes were requested, Li though summoned still did not come at once, but continued in private consultation with her mother.

sentences.zh: 先皇平昔或有幸禦，李氏嫉妒，令女巫李定奴作紙木人、鴛鴦符以事魘魅，致絕聖嗣。

translations.literal: Whenever the late Emperor had occasionally favored other women, Li was jealous; she had the witch Li Dingnu make paper-and-wood effigies and mandarin-duck talismans to work sorcery and haunting, causing the cutting off of the sage lineage.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the late Emperor had occasionally favored other women, Li was jealous; she had the witch Li Dingnu make paper-and-wood effigies and mandarin-duck talismans to work sorcery and haunting, causing the cutting off of the imperial line.

sentences.zh: 所為不軌，莫可殫陳。

translations.literal: Her unlawful acts cannot all be enumerated.
translations.idiomatic: Her unlawful acts cannot all be enumerated.

sentences.zh: 事既髮露，遣大臣按問，俱已款服。

translations.literal: Once the matter was exposed, chief ministers were sent to investigate; all have fully confessed.
translations.idiomatic: Once the matter was exposed, chief ministers were sent to investigate; all have fully confessed.

sentences.zh: 命宰臣往審，亦如之。

translations.literal: Ordered chief ministers to go and examine; likewise they confessed.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered chief ministers to go and interrogate them; they likewise confessed.

sentences.zh: 有司議，法當極刑。

translations.literal: The relevant offices deliberated; by law they should receive the extreme penalty.
translations.idiomatic: The responsible offices deliberated and held that, by law, the penalty should be death.

sentences.zh: 以其久侍先帝，欲免其死。

translations.literal: Because she had long served the late Emperor, (he) wished to spare her death.
translations.idiomatic: Because she had long attended the late Emperor, he wished to spare her life.

sentences.zh: 王公百僚，執奏堅確。

translations.literal: Princes, officials, and the hundred ministers submitted memorials firmly and resolutely.
translations.idiomatic: Princes, officials, and the entire court memorialized with adamant insistence.

sentences.zh: 今賜李氏自盡。

translations.literal: Now Li is granted to end her own life.
translations.idiomatic: Li was now granted permission to take her own life.

sentences.zh: 王盻兒、李新喜各正典刑。

translations.literal: Wang Pan'er and Li Xixin each received proper statutory punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Pan'er and Li Xixin were each executed according to law.

sentences.zh: 李氏兄安國軍節度使喜兒、弟少府監鐵哥如律，仍追除複系監籍，於遠地安置。

translations.literal: Li's elder brother Xier, Military Commissioner of the Anguo Army, and younger brother Tiege, Director of the Court of Imperial Manufactories, according to law; moreover their ranks were stripped and they were re-enrolled in the supervised registry and settled in a distant place.
translations.idiomatic: Li's elder brother Xier, Military Commissioner of the Anguo Army, and her younger brother Tiege, Director of the Court of Imperial Manufactories, were punished according to law; their offices were revoked, they were re-enrolled in the supervised registry, and exiled to a distant region.

sentences.zh: 諸連坐並依律令施行。

translations.literal: All those implicated by association were likewise carried out according to law and edicts.
translations.idiomatic: All who were implicated by association were punished according to law.

sentences.zh: 承禦賈氏亦賜自盡。」

translations.literal: Lady-in-Waiting Jia was also granted to end her own life."
translations.idiomatic: Lady-in-Waiting Jia was also granted permission to take her own life."

sentences.zh: 蓋章宗崩三日而稱範氏胎氣有損。

translations.literal: Probably only three days after Zhangzong's death they claimed Lady Fan's fetal qi was damaged.
translations.idiomatic: It seems that only three days after Zhangzong's death they already claimed that Lady Fan's fetal qi had been harmed.

sentences.zh: 章宗疾彌留，亦無完顏匡都提點中外事務敕旨。

translations.literal: When Zhangzong's illness was at the point of death, there was also no edict ordering Wanyan Kuang to oversee all affairs within and without.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhangzong lay at death's door, there was likewise no edict appointing Wanyan Kuang to oversee all affairs within and without the court.

sentences.zh: 或謂完顏匡欲奪定策功，構致如此。

translations.literal: Some say Wanyan Kuang wished to seize the merit of settling the succession and engineered matters thus.
translations.idiomatic: Some hold that Wanyan Kuang wished to claim the credit for settling the succession and deliberately contrived matters in this way.

sentences.zh: 自後天下不復稱元妃，但呼曰李師兒。

translations.literal: From then on the realm no longer called her First Consort, but only called her Li Shier.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter the realm no longer addressed her as First Consort; she was known only as Li Shier.

sentences.zh: 及胡沙虎弑衛王，立宣宗，請貶降衛王，降為東海郡侯。

translations.literal: When Hushahu assassinated Prince Wei and enthroned Xuanzong, he requested that Prince Wei be degraded; he was reduced to Marquis of Donghai Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When Hushahu assassinated Emperor Weishao and enthroned Emperor Xuanzong, he petitioned that Weishao be degraded to Marquis of Donghai Commandery.

sentences.zh: 其詔曰：「大安之初，頒諭天下，謂李氏與其母王盻兒及李新喜同謀，令賈氏虛稱有身，各正罪法。

translations.literal: The edict said: "At the beginning of Da'an, a proclamation was issued to the realm stating that Li together with her mother Wang Pan'er and Li Xixin conspired to have Lady Jia falsely claim pregnancy; each received proper punishment under the law.
translations.idiomatic: The edict read: "At the beginning of Da'an, an edict was promulgated throughout the realm declaring that Li, her mother Wang Pan'er, and Li Xixin had conspired to have Lady Jia falsely claim pregnancy; each was duly punished according to law.

sentences.zh: 朕惟章宗皇帝聖德聰明，豈容有此欺紿。

translations.literal: I consider that Emperor Zhangzong was sagely in virtue and keen in intelligence—how could such deception be tolerated?
translations.idiomatic: I reflect that Emperor Zhangzong was sagacious and clear-minded; how could such deception have been allowed?

sentences.zh: 近因集議，武衛軍副使兼提點近侍局完顏達、霍王傅大政德皆言賈氏事內有冤。

translations.literal: Recently at a collective deliberation, Wanyan Da, Vice Commissioner of the Martial Guard Army and concurrently overseer of the Inner Attendance Bureau, and Da Zhengde, Tutor to Prince Huo, both said that within the affair of Lady Jia there was injustice.
translations.idiomatic: At a recent assembly, Wanyan Da, Vice Commissioner of the Martial Guard Army and overseer of the Inner Attendance Bureau, and Da Zhengde, Tutor to Prince Huo, both testified that Lady Jia had been wronged.

sentences.zh: 此時，達職在近侍，政德護賈氏，所以知之。

translations.literal: At that time Da's post was in the inner attendance; Zhengde protected Lady Jia—therefore they knew.
translations.idiomatic: Da had served in the Inner Attendance Bureau at the time, and Zhengde had been Lady Jia's protector; that is how they knew.

sentences.zh: 朕親臨問佐證，其事暖昧無據，當時被罪貶責者可俱令放免還家。」

translations.literal: I personally inquired and corroborated; the matter was ambiguous without evidence; those who at the time were convicted and punished may all be ordered released and sent home."
translations.idiomatic: I personally examined witnesses and corroborating evidence and found the matter ambiguous and unsubstantiated; all who had been convicted and punished at the time are to be pardoned and sent home."

sentences.zh: 由是李氏家族皆得還。

translations.literal: Thereupon the Li clan all were able to return.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon the entire Li family was restored and allowed to return.

sentences.zh: 衛紹王后徒單氏，大安元年，立為皇后。

translations.literal: Queen Tudan of Emperor Weishao was established as empress in the first year of Da'an.
translations.idiomatic: Queen Tudan of Emperor Weishao was established as empress in the first year of Da'an.

sentences.zh: 至甯元年，胡沙虎亂，與衛王俱遷于衛邸。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhining, during Hushahu's rebellion, she was moved with Prince Wei to the Wei residence.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhining, during Hushahu's rebellion, she was moved with Prince Wei to the Wei residence.

sentences.zh: 帝遇弑，宣宗即位，衛王降為東海郡侯，徒單氏削皇后號。

translations.literal: The emperor was assassinated; Emperor Xuanzong took the throne; Prince Wei was demoted to Marquis of Donghai Commandery; Tudan's empress title was stripped.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was assassinated and Emperor Xuanzong took the throne. Prince Wei was demoted to Marquis of Donghai, and Tudan's empress title was stripped.

sentences.zh: 貞祐二年，遷都汴，詔凡衛紹王及鄗厲王家人皆徙鄭州，仍禁錮，不得出入。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhenyou, when the capital moved to Bian, an edict ordered that all the families of Prince Shao of Wei and Prince Li of Hao be moved to Zheng Prefecture and still kept under confinement, not permitted to go in or out.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhenyou, when the capital moved to Bian, an edict ordered the families of Prince Shao of Wei and Prince Li of Hao transferred to Zheng Prefecture and kept under confinement, forbidden to come or go.

sentences.zh: 男女不得婚嫁者十九年。

translations.literal: Men and women were not permitted to marry for nineteen years.
translations.idiomatic: For nineteen years men and women in the families were forbidden to marry.

sentences.zh: 天興元年，詔釋禁錮。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianxing, an edict released them from confinement.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Tianxing an edict released them from confinement.

sentences.zh: 是時，河南已不能守，子孫不知所終。

translations.literal: By then Henan could no longer be held; their descendants' fates are unknown.
translations.idiomatic: By then Henan could no longer be defended, and the fate of their descendants is unknown.

sentences.zh: 宣宗皇后王氏

translations.literal: Empress Wang of Emperor Xuanzong
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wang of Emperor Xuanzong

sentences.zh: 宣宗皇后王氏，中都人，明惠皇后妹也。

translations.literal: Empress Wang of Emperor Xuanzong, a native of the Central Capital, was the younger sister of Empress Minghui.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wang of Emperor Xuanzong was a native of the Central Capital and the younger sister of Empress Minghui.

sentences.zh: 其父微時嘗夢二玉梳化為月，已而生二后，及沒，有芝生於柩。

translations.literal: When her father was still obscure he once dreamed that two jade combs transformed into the moon; afterward two empresses were born; when he died, lingzhi fungus grew upon his coffin.
translations.idiomatic: While her father was still obscure, he once dreamed that two jade combs turned into the moon; afterward he fathered two daughters who became empresses, and when he died lingzhi fungus sprouted upon his coffin.

sentences.zh: 初，宣宗封翼王，章宗詔諸王求民家子，以廣繼嗣。

translations.literal: At first, when Xuanzong was enfeoffed as Prince Yi, Zhangzong ordered the princes to seek daughters of common families to broaden succession.
translations.idiomatic: Early on, when Xuanzong was enfeoffed as Prince Yi, Zhangzong ordered the princes to take commoners' daughters as consorts to broaden the imperial succession.

sentences.zh: 是時，后與龐氏偕入王邸，及見后姊有姿色，又納之。

translations.literal: At that time the empress and Lady Pang entered the princely residence together; seeing that the empress's elder sister had beauty, he also took her in.
translations.idiomatic: At that time she and Lady Pang entered the princely residence together; when he saw that her elder sister was beautiful, he took her in as well.

sentences.zh: 貞祐元年九月，封后為元妃，姊為淑妃，龐氏為真妃。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the first year of Zhenyou, the empress was enfeoffed as First Consort, her elder sister as Shufei, and Lady Pang as Zhenfei.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the first year of Zhenyou, she was created First Consort, her elder sister Shufei, and Lady Pang Zhenfei.

sentences.zh: 淑妃生哀宗，真妃生守純，后無子，養哀宗為己子。

translations.literal: Shufei bore Aizong; Zhenfei bore Shou Chun; the empress had no son and raised Aizong as her own child.
translations.idiomatic: Shufei bore Emperor Aizong, Zhenfei bore Shou Chun, and the empress, who had no children of her own, raised Aizong as her son.

sentences.zh: 貞祐二年七月，賜姓溫敦氏，立為皇后。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the second year of Zhenyou, she was granted the surname Wendun and established as empress.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the second year of Zhenyou, she was granted the surname Wendun and installed as empress.

sentences.zh: 追封后曾祖得壽司空、冀國公，曾祖母劉氏冀國夫人，祖璞司徒、益國公，祖母楊氏益國夫人，父彥昌太尉、汴國公，母馬氏汴國夫人。

translations.literal: Her great-grandfather Deshou was posthumously enfeoffed as Minister of Works and Duke of Ji State; her great-grandmother Lady Liu as Lady of Ji State; her grandfather Pu as Minister of Education and Duke of Yi State; her grandmother Lady Yang as Lady of Yi State; her father Yanchang as Grand Marshal and Duke of Bian State; her mother Lady Ma as Lady of Bian State.
translations.idiomatic: Her great-grandfather Deshou was posthumously enfeoffed Minister of Works and Duke of Ji; her great-grandmother, Lady Liu, Lady of Ji; her grandfather Pu, Minister of Education and Duke of Yi; her grandmother, Lady Yang, Lady of Yi; her father Yanchang, Grand Marshal and Duke of Bian; and her mother, Lady Ma, Lady of Bian.

sentences.zh: 三年，莊獻太子薨，哀宗為皇太子。

translations.literal: In the third year, Crown Prince Zhuangxian died; Aizong became crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year Crown Prince Zhuangxian died, and Aizong was made crown prince.

sentences.zh: 宣宗崩，哀宗即位。

translations.literal: Xuanzong died; Aizong ascended the throne.
translations.idiomatic: When Xuanzong died, Aizong ascended the throne.

sentences.zh: 正大元年，尊后為皇太后，號其宮曰仁聖，進封后父曰南陽郡王。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhengda, the empress was honored as Empress Dowager; her palace was styled Rensheng; her father was advanced in rank to Prince of Nanyang Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhengda she was honored as Empress Dowager; her palace was named Rensheng, and her father was enfeoffed Prince of Nanyang.

sentences.zh: 或曰：宣宗為諸王時，莊獻太子母為正妃，及即位，尊為皇后。

translations.literal: Some say: when Xuanzong was among the princes, the mother of Crown Prince Zhuangxian was Primary Consort; when he ascended the throne, she was honored as empress.
translations.idiomatic: Some accounts hold that when Xuanzong was still a prince, the mother of Crown Prince Zhuangxian was his primary consort, and that upon his accession she was elevated to empress.

sentences.zh: 貞祐元年九月，詔曰：「元妃某氏久奉侍於潛籓，已賜封於國號，可立為皇后。」

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the first year of Zhenyou an edict said: "First Consort So-and-so has long attended at the hidden princely establishment and has already been granted a title of state; she may be established as empress."
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the first year of Zhenyou an edict declared: "First Consort [Name] has long served at the prince's household and has already been granted a state title; she is hereby installed as empress."

sentences.zh: 其名氏蓋不可考也。

translations.literal: Her name and clan are probably beyond recovery.
translations.idiomatic: Her personal name and lineage can no longer be determined.

sentences.zh: 或又曰：自王氏姊妹入宮而后寵衰，尋為尼，王氏遂立為后，皆后姊明惠之謀也。

translations.literal: Some also say: from the time the Wang sisters entered the palace the former empress's favor declined; soon she became a nun, and the Wang was thereupon established as empress—all through the scheming of the empress's elder sister Minghui.
translations.idiomatic: Another account holds that after the Wang sisters entered the palace, the former consort's favor waned; she soon took vows as a nun, and Empress Wang was installed—all through the machinations of her elder sister Minghui.

sentences.zh: 初，王氏姊妹受封之日，大風昏霾，黃氣充塞天地。

translations.literal: At first, on the day the Wang sisters received their enfeoffments, great winds and murky haze filled heaven and earth with yellow qi.
translations.idiomatic: When the Wang sisters first received their titles, fierce winds and murky haze filled the heavens with yellow miasma.

sentences.zh: 已而，后夢丐者數萬踵其後，心甚惡之。

translations.literal: Before long the empress dreamed that tens of thousands of beggars followed at her heels; her heart greatly loathed it.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward the empress dreamed that tens of thousands of beggars trailed behind her, and the dream sickened her.

sentences.zh: 占者曰：「后者，天下之母也。

translations.literal: The diviner said: "The empress is the mother of the realm.
translations.idiomatic: A diviner said: "The empress is mother to the realm.

sentences.zh: 百姓貧窶，將誰訴焉？」

translations.literal: The common people are poor and destitute—to whom will they appeal?"
translations.idiomatic: When the people are destitute, to whom will they turn for redress?"

sentences.zh: 后遂敕有司，京城設粥與冰藥。

translations.literal: The empress thereupon ordered the offices to set out gruel and cooling medicines in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: The empress thereupon ordered the authorities to distribute gruel and cooling medicines throughout the capital.

sentences.zh: 及壬辰、癸巳歲，河南饑饉。

translations.literal: By the years renchen and guisi, Henan suffered famine.
translations.idiomatic: In the renchen and guisi years famine struck Henan.

sentences.zh: 大元兵圍汴，加以大疫，汴城之民，死者百余萬，后皆目睹焉。

translations.literal: The Great Yuan army besieged Bian; added to this was a great pestilence; among the people of Bian city more than a million died; the empress witnessed it all.
translations.idiomatic: When the armies of the Great Yuan besieged Bian and plague swept the city, more than a million people in the capital perished; the empress saw it all with her own eyes.

sentences.zh: 哀宗釋服，將禘饗太廟，先期，有司奏冕服成，上請仁聖、慈聖兩宮太后禦內殿，因試衣之以見，兩宮大悅。

translations.literal: When Aizong ended mourning and was about to perform the di offering at the Grand Ancestral Temple, in advance the offices reported that sacrificial robes were finished; the Emperor invited the Empresses Dowager of Rensheng and Cisheng palaces to attend the inner hall and tried on the robes for them to see; both palaces were greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: When Aizong completed mourning and prepared to perform the di rite at the Grand Ancestral Temple, the relevant offices reported in advance that the ceremonial robes were ready. The emperor invited the Empresses Dowager of the Rensheng and Cisheng palaces to the inner hall and had the robes tried on for their inspection; both were delighted.

sentences.zh: 上更便服，奉觴為兩宮壽。

translations.literal: The Emperor then changed to informal dress and raised a cup to wish long life to both palaces.
translations.idiomatic: He then changed into informal dress and raised a cup to toast the long life of both empresses dowager.

sentences.zh: 仁聖太后諭上曰：「祖宗初取天下甚不易。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager of Rensheng Palace admonished the Emperor: "The ancestors at first took the realm with great difficulty.
translations.idiomatic: The Rensheng Empress Dowager admonished him: "Our ancestors won the realm only with great hardship.

sentences.zh: 何時使四方承平，百姓安樂，天子服此法服，于中都祖廟行禘饗乎？」

translations.literal: When will the four quarters enjoy enduring peace and the common people live in security and joy, so that the Son of Heaven may wear these law-garments and perform the di offering at the ancestral temple in the Central Capital?"
translations.idiomatic: When will the four quarters know lasting peace and the people live in ease, so that the Son of Heaven may don these robes and perform the di rite at the ancestral temple in the Central Capital?"

sentences.zh: 上曰：「阿婆有此意，臣亦何嘗忘。」

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "Grandmother holds this intent; your subject, too, has never forgotten."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied: "Grandmother thinks as I do; I have never ceased to cherish this hope."

sentences.zh: 慈聖太后亦曰：「恆有此心，則見此當有期矣。」

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager of Cisheng Palace also said: "If one always holds this heart, then seeing this must have its appointed time."
translations.idiomatic: The Cisheng Empress Dowager added: "So long as we keep this wish alive, the day we see it fulfilled must surely come."

sentences.zh: 遂酌酒為上壽，歡然而罷。

translations.literal: They thereupon poured wine to wish the Emperor long life, and joyfully dispersed.
translations.idiomatic: They then poured wine to toast the emperor's long life, and the gathering broke up in good cheer.

sentences.zh: 天興元年冬，哀宗遷歸德。

translations.literal: In the winter of the first year of Tianxing, Emperor Aizong moved to Guide.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the first year of Tianxing, Emperor Aizong moved the court to Guide.

sentences.zh: 二年正月，遣近侍徒單四喜、術甲荅失不奉迎兩宮。

translations.literal: In the first month of the second year, he sent close attendants Tudan Sixi and Shujia Dashibu to welcome the two palaces.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the second year he sent close attendants Tudan Sixi and Shujia Dashibu to welcome the two empresses dowager.

sentences.zh: 后禦仁安殿，出鋌金及七寶金洗，分賜從行忠孝軍。

translations.literal: The empress attended at Ren'an Hall, brought out ingot gold and seven-treasure gold basins, and distributed them among the Loyal and Filial Army accompanying the journey.
translations.idiomatic: The empress attended at Ren'an Hall, brought out ingot gold and seven-treasure gold basins, and distributed them among the Loyal and Filial Army accompanying the journey.

sentences.zh: 是夜，兩宮及柔妃裴滿氏等乘馬出宮，行至陳留，城左右火起，疑有兵，不敢進。

translations.literal: That night the two palaces, Gentle Consort Peiman, and others rode out of the palace; reaching Chenliu, fires rose on both sides of the city; suspecting troops, they dared not advance.
translations.idiomatic: That night the two empresses dowager, Gentle Consort Peiman, and others rode out of the palace. When they reached Chenliu, fires flared on both sides of the city; fearing an ambush, they dared not advance.

sentences.zh: 后亟命還宮。

translations.literal: The empress urgently ordered a return to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: The empress urgently ordered a return to the palace.

sentences.zh: 明日，入京憩四喜家。

translations.literal: The next day they entered the capital and rested at Sixi's home.
translations.idiomatic: The next day they entered the capital and rested at Sixi's home.

sentences.zh: 少頃，輦迎入宮。

translations.literal: Before long an imperial carriage welcomed them back into the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Before long an imperial carriage brought them back into the palace.

sentences.zh: 方謀再行，京城破，后及諸妃嬪北遷，不知所終。

translations.literal: Just as they were planning to set out again, the capital fell; the empress and the various consorts and concubines moved north, their fates unknown.
translations.idiomatic: Just as they were planning to set out again, the capital fell. The empress and the consorts and concubines moved north, and their fates are unknown.

sentences.zh: 惟寶符李氏從至宣德州，居摩訶院。

translations.literal: Only Lady Li of Baofu followed as far as Xuande Prefecture and dwelt in Mohe Courtyard.
translations.idiomatic: Only Lady Li of Baofu followed as far as Xuande Prefecture and lived in Mohe Courtyard.

sentences.zh: 李氏自入院，止寢佛殿中，作為幡旆。

translations.literal: From the time Lady Li entered the courtyard, she slept only in the Buddha hall and made banners and pennants.
translations.idiomatic: From the time she entered the courtyard, Lady Li slept only in the Buddha hall and made banners and pennants.

sentences.zh: 會當同后妃北行，將發，佛像前自縊死，且自書門紙曰「寶符禦侍此處身故。」

translations.literal: When the time came to travel north with the empresses and consorts, just before departure she hanged herself before the Buddha image and wrote on the door paper: "Baofu the imperial attendant died here."
translations.idiomatic: When the time came to travel north with the empresses and consorts, just before departure she hanged herself before the Buddha image and wrote on the door paper, "Baofu the imperial attendant died here."

sentences.zh: 宣宗明惠皇后

translations.literal: Empress Minghui of Emperor Xuanzong
translations.idiomatic: Empress Minghui of Emperor Xuanzong

sentences.zh: 宣宗明惠皇后，王皇后之姊也。

translations.literal: Empress Minghui of Emperor Xuanzong was the elder sister of Empress Wang.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Minghui of Emperor Xuanzong was the elder sister of Empress Wang.

sentences.zh: 生哀宗。

translations.literal: She bore Aizong.
translations.idiomatic: She was the birth mother of Emperor Aizong.

sentences.zh: 宣宗即位，封為淑妃。

translations.literal: When Xuanzong ascended the throne, she was enfeoffed as Shufei.
translations.idiomatic: When Xuanzong took the throne, she was created Shufei.

sentences.zh: 及妹立為后，進封元妃。

translations.literal: When her younger sister was established as empress, she was advanced to First Consort.
translations.idiomatic: When her younger sister was made empress, she was promoted to First Consort.

sentences.zh: 哀宗即位，詔尊為皇太后，號其宮曰慈聖。

translations.literal: When Aizong ascended the throne, an edict honored her as Empress Dowager; her palace was styled Cisheng.
translations.idiomatic: When Aizong ascended the throne, she was honored as Empress Dowager and her palace named Cisheng.

sentences.zh: 后性端嚴，頗達古今。

translations.literal: The empress was by nature dignified and strict, and well versed in affairs ancient and modern.
translations.idiomatic: The empress was dignified and strict by nature, and well versed in affairs ancient and modern.

sentences.zh: 哀宗已立為皇太子，有過尚切責之，及即位，始免郐賈楚。

translations.literal: When Aizong had already been established as crown prince, she still sternly reproved him for faults; only after he took the throne did she pardon Guo Jiachu.
translations.idiomatic: Even after Aizong had been made crown prince, she sternly reproved him for his faults; only after he took the throne did she pardon Guo Jiachu.

sentences.zh: 一日，宮中就食，尚器有玉碗楪三，一奉太后，二奉帝及中宮。

translations.literal: One day, while dining in the palace, the table service had three jade bowls and dishes: one for the empress dowager, two for the emperor and the central palace.
translations.idiomatic: One day at a palace meal the table service held three jade bowls and dishes: one for the empress dowager and two for the emperor and empress.

sentences.zh: 荊王母真妃龐氏以瑪瑙器進食，后見之怒，召主者責曰：「誰令汝妄生分別，荊王母豈卑我兒婦耶。

translations.literal: Prince Jing's mother, True Consort Lady Pang, presented food in agate vessels; the empress saw this and grew angry; she summoned the steward and reproved him, saying: "Who told you to make distinctions without warrant? Is Prince Jing's mother beneath my daughter-in-law?
translations.idiomatic: Prince Jing's mother, True Consort Lady Pang, presented food in agate vessels. The empress grew angry, summoned the steward, and reproved him: "Who told you to make distinctions without warrant? Is Prince Jing's mother beneath my daughter-in-law?

sentences.zh: 非飲食細故，已令有司杖殺汝矣。」

translations.literal: Had this not been a mere matter of food and drink, I would already have ordered the authorities to beat you to death."
translations.idiomatic: Had this not been a mere matter of food and drink, I would already have ordered the authorities to beat you to death."

sentences.zh: 是後，宮中奉真妃有加。

translations.literal: Thereafter within the palace True Consort was treated with added honor.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter True Consort was treated with added honor within the palace.

sentences.zh: 或告荊王謀不軌者，下獄，議已決。

translations.literal: Someone reported that Prince Jing plotted sedition; he was imprisoned and the case was decided.
translations.idiomatic: Someone reported that Prince Jing plotted sedition. He was imprisoned and the case was decided.

sentences.zh: 帝言於后，后曰：「汝止一兄，奈何以讒言欲害之。

translations.literal: The emperor spoke to the empress; the empress said: "You have only one elder brother—how can you wish to harm him on the basis of slander?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor spoke to the empress. She said, "You have only one elder brother—how can you wish to harm him on the basis of slander?

sentences.zh: 章宗殺伯與叔，享年不永，皇嗣又絕，何為欲效之耶。

translations.literal: Zhangzong killed his uncles, did not live long, and the imperial line was cut off—why would you wish to imitate that?
translations.idiomatic: Zhangzong killed his uncles, did not live long, and the imperial line was cut off—why would you wish to imitate that?

sentences.zh: 趣赦出，使來見我。

translations.literal: Hurry and pardon him, and have him come to see me.
translations.idiomatic: Hurry and pardon him, and have him come to see me.

sentences.zh: 移時不至，吾不見汝矣。」

translations.literal: If after a while he does not arrive, I shall not see you."
translations.idiomatic: If he does not come soon, I shall not see you."

sentences.zh: 帝起，后立待，王至，涕泣慰撫之。

translations.literal: The emperor rose; the empress stood waiting; when the prince arrived, she wept and comforted him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor rose. The empress stood waiting, and when the prince arrived she wept and comforted him.

sentences.zh: 哀宗甚寵一宮人，欲立為后。

translations.literal: Aizong greatly favored a palace woman and wished to establish her as empress.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Aizong deeply favored a palace woman and wished to make her empress.

sentences.zh: 后惡其微賤，固命出之。

translations.literal: The empress hated her humble status and firmly ordered her removed.
translations.idiomatic: The empress, disgusted by her low birth, insisted that she be removed from court.

sentences.zh: 上不得已，命放之出宮，語使者曰：「爾出東華門，不計何人，首遇者即賜之。」

translations.literal: The Emperor had no choice; he ordered her released from the palace and told the envoy: "When you go out Donghua Gate, heed not who it is—the first person you meet, grant her to him as wife."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, unable to refuse, ordered her released from the palace and told the envoy: "Leave by the Donghua Gate. Whoever you meet first—no matter who he is—give her to him as his wife."

sentences.zh: 於是遇一販繒者，遂賜為妻。

translations.literal: Thereupon he met a peddler of silk and granted her to him as wife.
translations.idiomatic: He met a silk peddler and gave her to him in marriage.

sentences.zh: 點檢撒合輦教上騎鞠，后傳旨戒之雲：「汝為人臣，當輔主以正，顧乃教之戲耶。

translations.literal: Inspector Sahe Nian taught the Emperor to ride and play cuju; the empress sent a decree of warning saying: "You are a minister—you should assist your lord in the right; yet you teach him sport?
translations.idiomatic: Inspector Sahe Nian taught the emperor polo; the empress sent a reprimand: "You are a subject of the throne. You ought to guide your sovereign toward rectitude—yet you teach him games?

sentences.zh: 再有聞，必大杖汝矣。」

translations.literal: If I hear of this again, I shall surely have you beaten severely."
translations.idiomatic: If I hear of this again, you will be thrashed within an inch of your life."

sentences.zh: 比年小捷，國勢頗振，文士有奏賦頌以聖德中興為言者。

translations.literal: In recent years there were small victories; the state's fortunes revived somewhat; literary men submitted fu and eulogies speaking of sagely virtue and restoration.
translations.idiomatic: In recent years the dynasty had won minor victories and the state's fortunes had revived somewhat; literati submitted encomia celebrating a sagely restoration.

sentences.zh: 后聞不悅曰：「帝年少氣銳，無懼心則驕怠生。

translations.literal: The empress heard and was displeased, saying: "The Emperor is young and spirited; without fear in the heart, arrogance and slackness arise.
translations.idiomatic: The empress heard of this and said disapprovingly: "The emperor is young and high-spirited; without a healthy fear of failure, arrogance and sloth will follow.

sentences.zh: 今幸一勝，何等中興，而若輩諂之如是。」

translations.literal: Now, having fortunately won one victory, what sort of restoration is this—and you people flatter him thus!"
translations.idiomatic: One skirmish won, and you call it a restoration? The flattery is shameless."

sentences.zh: 正大八年九月丙申，后崩，遺命園陵制度，務從儉約。

translations.literal: On bingshen of the ninth month of the eighth year of Zhengda the empress died; her final instructions on the park-tomb regulations demanded utmost frugality.
translations.idiomatic: On bingshen day of the ninth month in the eighth year of Zhengda the empress died, leaving instructions that her tomb and park be kept as simple as possible.

sentences.zh: 十二月己未，葬汴城迎朔門外五裏莊獻太子墓之西。

translations.literal: On jiwei of the twelfth month she was buried five li outside Yingshuo Gate of Bian city, west of Crown Prince Zhuangxian's tomb.
translations.idiomatic: On jiwei day of the twelfth month she was buried five li outside the Yingshuo Gate of Bian, to the west of Crown Prince Zhuangxian's tomb.

sentences.zh: 諡明惠皇后。

translations.literal: She was posthumously titled Empress Minghui.
translations.idiomatic: She was posthumously honored as Empress Minghui.

sentences.zh: 哀宗皇后，徒單氏。

translations.literal: Empress of Emperor Aizong, of the Tudan clan.
translations.idiomatic: The empress of Emperor Aizong was of the Tudan clan.

sentences.zh: 宣宗及后有疾，后嘗刲膚以進，宣宗聞而嘉之。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuanzong and the empress were ill, she once cut her own flesh to present as medicine; Emperor Xuanzong heard of it and praised her.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuanzong and the empress fell ill, she once cut her own flesh to present as medicine; Emperor Xuanzong heard of it and praised her.

sentences.zh: 興定四年，后父鎮南軍節度使頑僧有罪，宣宗以后純孝，因曲赦之，聽其致仕。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Xingding, the empress's father Wanseng, Military Commissioner of the Zhennan Army, was guilty of a crime; Emperor Xuanzong, because of the empress's pure filial devotion, thereupon pardoned him by special grace and permitted him to retire.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Xingding the empress's father Wanseng, Military Commissioner of the Zhennan Army, was guilty of a crime. Because of the empress's filial devotion, Emperor Xuanzong pardoned him by special grace and allowed him to retire.

sentences.zh: 正大元年，詔立為皇后。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhengda, an edict established her as empress.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhengda an edict established her as empress.

sentences.zh: 哀宗遷歸德，遣后弟四喜等詣汴奉迎，夜至陳留，不敢進，複歸於汴。

translations.literal: When Aizong moved to Guide, he sent the empress's younger brother Sixi and others to Bian to welcome her; by night they reached Chenliu, dared not advance, and returned again to Bian.
translations.idiomatic: When Aizong moved to Guide, he sent the empress's younger brother Sixi and others to Bian to welcome her. They reached Chenliu by night, dared not advance, and returned to Bian.

sentences.zh: 未幾，城破北遷，不知所終。

translations.literal: Before long the city fell; she moved north, her fate unknown.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the city fell; she moved north, and her fate is unknown.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：《周禮》「九嬪，掌婦學之法，婦德、婦言、婦容、婦功。」

translations.literal: Commentary: The Rites of Zhou states: "The Nine Consorts administer the methods of women's learning—womanly virtue, womanly speech, womanly deportment, and womanly work."
translations.idiomatic: Commentary: The Rites of Zhou states, "The Nine Consorts preside over the instruction of palace women in four arts: virtue, speech, deportment, and work."

sentences.zh: 班昭氏論之曰：「婦德，不必才明絕異也。

translations.literal: Ban Zhao wrote on this: "Womanly virtue does not require exceptional talent and brilliance.
translations.idiomatic: Ban Zhao observed: "Womanly virtue need not rest on extraordinary talent or brilliance.

sentences.zh: 婦言，不必便口利辭也。

translations.literal: Womanly speech does not require a fluent and glib tongue.
translations.idiomatic: Womanly speech need not be quick and clever of tongue.

sentences.zh: 婦容，不必顏色美麗也。

translations.literal: Womanly deportment does not require beautiful countenance.
translations.idiomatic: Womanly deportment need not depend on physical beauty.

sentences.zh: 婦功，不必功巧過人也。

translations.literal: Womanly work does not require craftsmanship surpassing others.
translations.idiomatic: Womanly work need not exceed all others in skill and dexterity.

sentences.zh: 清閒貞靜，守節整齊，行己有恥，動靜有法，是謂婦德。

translations.literal: Clear, at ease, chaste, and tranquil; keeping to rectitude and order; conducting oneself with shame; in movement and stillness observing law—this is called womanly virtue.
translations.idiomatic: To be pure, serene, chaste, and calm; to observe propriety; to act with a sense of shame; to comport oneself with decorum in every motion and rest—this is womanly virtue.

sentences.zh: 擇辭而說，不道惡語，時然後言，不厭於人，是謂婦言。

translations.literal: Choose words and speak; do not utter evil speech; speak only when the time is right; do not weary others—this is called womanly speech.
translations.idiomatic: To choose one's words, speak no ill, speak only when the occasion demands, and never weary others with one's voice—this is womanly speech.

sentences.zh: 盥浣塵穢，服飾鮮潔，沐浴以時，身不垢辱，是謂婦容。

translations.literal: Wash away filth, keep garments fresh and clean, bathe at the proper times, let the body know no disgrace of dirt—this is called womanly deportment.
translations.idiomatic: To keep oneself clean, dress neatly, bathe at the proper hour, and never appear before others in disarray—this is womanly deportment.

sentences.zh: 專心紡績，不好戲笑，潔齊酒食，以奉賓客，是謂婦功。」

translations.literal: Devote the heart to spinning and weaving; do not delight in sport and laughter; keep wine and food pure and orderly to serve guests—this is called womanly work."
translations.idiomatic: To devote oneself to weaving, shun frivolity, and keep food and drink in good order for the entertainment of guests—this is womanly work."

sentences.zh: 後世婦學不修，麗色以相高，巧言以相傾，銜能以市恩，逢迎以固寵。

translations.literal: In later ages women's learning was not cultivated; beautiful color was used to vie for superiority, cunning speech to overthrow one another, hoarded ability to market favor, and flattery to secure affection.
translations.idiomatic: In later ages the arts of womanhood were neglected. Women competed in beauty, undermined one another with clever speech, traded on talent to win favor, and courted their lords to hold their place.

sentences.zh: 是故悼平掣頓皇統，以隕其身，海陵蠱惑群嬖，幾亡其國。

translations.literal: Therefore Empress Daoping checked and stalled the imperial lineage and lost her life; Hailing bewitched his flock of favorites and nearly lost the state.
translations.idiomatic: Thus Empress Daoping hamstrung the imperial line and lost her life; Hailing seduced a host of favorites and nearly destroyed the dynasty.

sentences.zh: 道陵李氏擅寵蠹政，卒憤其宗。

translations.literal: Li of Daoling monopolized favor and corrupted government, and in the end brought ruin upon her clan.
translations.idiomatic: Li, consort of the Daoling Emperor, monopolized imperial favor, corrupted the government, and in the end brought her own house to ruin.

sentences.zh: 嗚呼，可不戒哉。

translations.literal: Alas—can one fail to take warning?
translations.idiomatic: Alas—is there not a lesson here?

translations.idiomatic: "Meng'an" is also rendered "Ming'an" or "Ming An"; in Jurchen it means "thousand" and probably denotes a commander of a thousand men.
